title: Impact of artificial intelligence on project planning, scheduling, and control
abstractText: Abstract The growing complexity of engineering and construction projects has revealed the weaknesses of conventional project planning, scheduling, and control approaches. Traditional tools often employ fixed assumptions, deterministic models, and past averages, which are inadequate for dealing with uncertainty, dynamic environments, and large-scale data. Artificial intelligence has become a disruptive technology that can be used to improve decision-making, prediction, and automation in project management processes. This paper examines the application of artificial intelligence in project planning, scheduling, and control within the engineering and construction sector. The paper summarises the application of artificial intelligence methods, including machine learning, optimization algorithms, and predictive analytics, in enhancing project performance using a methodical review of the recent scholarly literature and industry practise. The results show that artificial intelligence promotes the planning accuracy, flexibility of scheduling, and real-time project control to a great extent, as it allows data-driven insights and flexible responses. Issues of data quality, company preparedness, and ethical issues are major obstacles to implementation. The research paper adds to the project management literature because it develops the application of artificial intelligence in the three fundamental project management functions and provides practical advice to practitioners interested in introducing intelligent project management systems. Keywords Artificial intelligence, project planning, project scheduling, project control, construction management, digital transformation

title: Pelatihan Strategi Pengelolaan Usaha Bermodal Kecil Bagi Wirausaha Muda Lokabisa Bojonggede
abstractText: Kegiatan PKM dilaksanakan untuk memperkuat kemampuan wirausaha muda dalam mengelola usaha dengan modal terbatas, Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan pemahaman peserta mengenai strategi praktis pengelolaan usaha dan mendukung perencanaan bisnis yang lebih terstruktur bagi anggota komunitas Lokabisa Bojonggede, Kabupaten Bogor. Kegiatan dilaksanakan secara luring pada 26 September 2026 dengan pendekatan pelatihan partisipatif melalui pemaparan materi, diskusi, studi kasus, simulasi perhitungan usaha, dan penyusunan rencana usaha sederhana satu halaman. Materi meliputi identifikasi peluang usaha, perencanaan modal, pencatatan keuangan sederhana, perhitungan Harga Pokok Penjualan (HPP), penetapan harga jual, dan pemasaran digital berbiaya rendah. Evaluasi dilakukan berdasarkan kuesioner setelah kegiatan yang diisi oleh 13 responden. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa persepsi manfaat kegiatan memperoleh nilai rata-rata 4,69 dari skala 5, sedangkan kepuasan keseluruhan mencapai 4,54. Penyampaian materi oleh tutor memperoleh nilai rata-rata 4,62 dan materi pelatihan 4,46. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa peserta memberikan respons positif dan menilai kegiatan bermanfaat. Kegiatan selanjutnya disarankan dilengkapi dengan tes sebelum dan sesudah pelatihan, penilaian rencana usaha, serta pendampingan lanjutan untuk mengevaluasi penerapan dan keberlanjutan hasil pelatihan.

title: Analisis Deskriptif Profitabilitas PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk Tahun 2021-2025: Mengidentifikasi Pola Kenaikan/Penurunan dan Interpretasi Manajerial
abstractText: Penelitian dilakukan untuk menganalisis perkembangan profitabilitas PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk periode 2021-2025 berdasarkan biaya, laba, dan segmen usaha. Penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan pendekatan deskriptif. Data sekunder bersumber dari laporan keuangan konsolidasian dan laporan tahunan Perusahaan, lalu dianalisis melalui rasio COGS, beban operasional, markup, gross profit margin (GPM), operating profit margin (OPM), net profit margin (NPM), return on assets (ROA), dan return on equity (ROE). Hasil menunjukkan bahwa penjualan naik 35,3% selama periode pengamatan, tetapi profitabilitas menurun pada 2022-2023 dan pulih pada 2024-2025. GPM turun dari 17,87% pada 2021 menjadi 14,68% pada 2023, lalu mencapai 21,73% pada 2025. Pola serupa terjadi pada OPM (7,85%; 4,31%; 10,18%), NPM (4,75%; 1,85%; 7,05%), ROA, dan ROE. Penurunan margin terjadi ketika penjualan masih tumbuh, sehingga mengindikasikan tekanan pada biaya produksi, bukan permintaan. Peternakan komersial dan pakan ternak menyumbang sekitar 65% penjualan 2025, sedangkan segmen pengolahan hasil peternakan dan produk konsumen tumbuh paling cepat. Karena COGS dialokasikan secara proporsional, efisiensi antarsegmen belum dapat dinilai. Pengendalian biaya bahan baku menjadi prioritas manajemen untuk menjaga profitabilitas.

title: Silyl Chloroalkenyl and Alkynyl Sulfur Pentafluorides as Versatile Reagents to Access Fundamental SF5 Building Blocks
abstractText: Abstract Herein, we report a second-generation SF5-alkenyl platform reagent granting facile benchtop access to a variety of known and unknown SF5-containing building blocks under mild conditions without any necessity to use pentafluorosulfanylation reagents, such as SF5Cl, on-site. This work overcomes the previous synthetic bottleneck that had prevented a broader use of the triisopropylsilylalkynyl (TASP) reagent. This versatile platform reagent is thermally stable, easy to handle, shows high shelf stability, and can be accessed on a multigram scale. This class of reagents undergoes protodesilylation/nucleophilic substitution reactions with O-, S-, and N-nucleophiles allowing access to (E)-configured α-SF5-enamines (up to >99%), (E)-configured α-SF5-vinyl ethers (up to 90%), another synthetically useful access to (E)-configured β-vinyl sulfides (up to 99%), O,O-acetals (up to 95%), and S,S-acetals (up to 97%) in a single reaction step. Further processing allowed access to S,S-ketene acetals (up to 97%), the corresponding α-SF5-acetic acid esters (up to 88%), as well as α-SF5-acetic acid (92%). Based on these findings, we shed light on the operating reaction mechanism by DFT studies, revealing that the amount of charge accumulated on the α-SF5 carbon controls the efficacy of the reaction with different nucleophiles. In a second part, we reconnected to previous inaccessible alkynyl sulfur pentafluorides by developing a novel in situ elimination strategy and identified the TBDMS derivative as an accessible, stable, and reactive reagent to prepare the complementary (Z)-configured β-vinyl sulfides (up to 85%) in a single reaction step, whereas the pure TMS and TES alkynyl derivatives were found to be inaccessible or unstable under ambient conditions. This report offers a versatile and robust protocol to access important SF5-containing organic motifs employing a commercially available prefunctionalized SF5 reagent.

title: ActiNet: an open-source tool for activity intensity classification of wrist-worn accelerometry using self-supervised deep learning
abstractText: Abstract The use of accurate and reliable open-source human activity recognition (HAR) models on passively collected wrist-accelerometer data is essential in large-scale epidemiological studies that investigate the association between physical activity and health outcomes. While self-supervised learning has generated considerable excitement in improving HAR, the extent to which these models, coupled with hidden Markov models (HMMs), would make a tangible improvement to classification performance and the effect this may have on the predicted daily activity intensity compositions is unknown. Using up to 24 h of wrist-worn accelerometer data from 151 CAPTURE-24 participants (aged 18–91, mean age 42, 66% female), we trained the ActiNet model, consisting of HARNet, a self-supervised, 18-layer, modified ResNet-V2 model, followed by hidden Markov model (HMM) smoothing, to classify labels of activity intensity. The performance of this model, evaluated using fivefold stratified group cross-validation, was then compared to a baseline random forest (RF) + HMM, established in existing literature. Differences in performance and classification outputs were compared with different subgroups of age and sex within the CAPTURE-24 population. The ActiNet model was able to distinguish labels of activity intensity with a mean macro F1 score of 0.82 and a mean Cohen’s kappa score of 0.86. This exceeded the performance of the RF + HMM, trained and validated on the same dataset, with mean scores of 0.76 and 0.80, respectively. The improvements in performance were consistent across subgroups of age and sex. These findings encourage the use of ActiNet for the extraction of activity intensity labels from wrist-accelerometer data in future epidemiological studies.

title: Cycle holonomy captures higher-order compatibility constraints in remote synchronization
abstractText: Higher-order interactions have typically been modeled using hypergraphs or simplicial complexes, where interactions explicitly involve more than two nodes. Here we demonstrate that effective higher-order dynamical constraints emerge naturally on ordinary graphs, provided the interaction carries nontrivial topological structure. We study a gauge-coupled phase model with edge phase lags whose accumulation around closed loops produces gauge-invariant mismatches. We show that the associated twisted Laplacian admits a zero mode if and only if all cycle holonomies vanish. Consequently, global compatibility is obstructed not by local pairwise mismatches, but by intrinsic topological frustration on cycles. We then connect this framework to the symmetric Sakaguchi--Kuramoto model, whose local coupling law differs from the gauge-coupled model but whose node phases impose cycle closure on physical phase differences. For cactus graphs, path mismatches induced by the symmetric lag can be represented through associated cycle holonomies, providing a static spectral encoding of their global residual incompatibility. Our results establish a spectral framework linking frustration to cycle-level constraints and identify cycle holonomy as a local-to-global diagnostic of path incompatibility in synchronization dynamics.

title: Employing “FAST Water” to Accelerate Self-Assembly
abstractText: Abstract Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are a powerful tool for elucidating the molecular mechanisms of supramolecular self-assembly, but the long time scales of aggregation often make all-atom simulations computationally challenging. Here, we evaluate the recently developed TIP3P-FAST water model as a simple strategy to accelerate self-assembly simulations in an aqueous solution. TIP3P-FAST employs mass repartitioning and rescaling within a water molecule, increasing the molecular mobility without altering the underlying potential energy surface. We investigate three representative self-assembling systems with distinct aggregation mechanisms and resulting morphologies: l-phenylalanine tripeptide (FFF), methyl-substituted ureido-pyrimidinone (UPy), and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). Simulations of isolated solutes reveal an around 2.5-fold increase in diffusion coefficients in TIP3P-FAST water compared to conventional TIP3P water, while solvent-accessible surface areas, radial distribution functions, hydrogen-bond numbers, and interaction energies remain unchanged. Self-assembly simulations initiated from dispersed monomers show markedly accelerated aggregation kinetics in FAST water, as evidenced by a faster decrease in solvent-accessible surface area and the number of clusters. For UPy, enhanced dynamics facilitate more efficient structural reorganization, yielding assemblies with characteristics comparable to or even more ordered than those obtained in TIP3P water at the same interval. These results demonstrate that TIP3P-FAST substantially reduces the computational cost of atomistic self-assembly simulations while preserving the equilibrium structural and thermodynamic properties, providing a practical route for studying complex supramolecular systems.

Non-thermal effects and temperature disparities in uniform supersonic flows
abstractText: Abstract Over the last 40 years, low-temperature reaction rate coefficients in astrochemical databases have largely come from CRESU ( Cinétique de Réaction en Ecoulement Supersonique Uniforme ) experiments, where the flow is described by a single temperature under an assumption of local thermal equilibrium. Here we directly test this assumption using infrared frequency comb spectroscopy, laser-induced fluorescence, Pitot measurements, and computational fluid dynamics in seeded supersonic flows. We observe persistent vibrational excitation in carbonyl sulfide (OCS) and nitrous oxide (N 2 O) under all conditions examined, despite efficient rotational cooling, demonstrating a breakdown of local thermal equilibrium within the flow. In parallel, we find that conventional Pitot-derived temperatures do not consistently reflect the energetic state of the reacting ensemble. These results show that the reacting ensemble in CRESU flows cannot always be described by a single thermodynamic temperature, particularly for species with low-lying vibrational modes, and that internal-state distributions should be carefully considered when interpreting low-temperature reaction rate coefficients in astrochemical kinetic databases.

A Thematic Mapping Approach to Stunting Segmentation in Indonesia by Province Using Finite Mixture Partial Least Squares Method
abstractText: Stunting remains one of Indonesia’s most persistent public-health problems, and the nationalprevalence conceals subtantial variation across the country’s 38 provinces. This study modelsseven latent constructs behind stunting, antenatal care, early initiation of breastfeeding,immunization, sanitation, exclusive breastfeeding, low birth weight, and stunting using PartialLeast Squares Structural Equation Modeling on 2023–2024 provincial health-profile datapublished by Indonesia’s Ministry of Health, and then applies Finite Mixture Partial LeastSquares (FIMIX-PLS) to detect unobserved heterogeneity across provinces and to translate theresulting segments into a thematic map. The measurement model satisfied every recommendedvalidity and reliability threshold, with an Average Variance Extracted between 0.835 and0.932 and both Cronbach’s alpha and composite reliability above 0.80. In the pooled nationalmodel, low birth weight was the only construct with a statistically significant direct path tostunting (β = 0.540, p .001); antenatal care showed no significant direct path to stunting(β = −0.143, p = .678) but exerted a significant total effect (β = −0.365) entirely through afully mediated pathway via low birth weight (indirect effect β = −0.263, p = .022), togetherexplaining 63.0% of the variance in stunting. Model-selection criteria favored a three-segmentsolution comprising 21, 10, and 7 provinces, dominated respectively by sanitation-related,birth-weight-related, and breastfeeding-related structural pathways. Mapping these segmentsgeographically shows that provinces sharing a dominant pathway are not scattered at randombut tend to cluster by region, indicating that stunting-reduction programs should be tailoredto each segment’s dominant pathway rather than applied uniformly across the whole country.

title: Diabetes Risk Prediction under Severe Class Imbalance: Comparing Firth Logistic Regression and SMOTEN-Based Logistic Regression
abstractText: Diabetes mellitus is a major noncommunicable disease, and reliable early-detection prediction can support Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 3.4. This study compares standard logistic regression, Firth's Penalized Logistic Regression, and SMOTEN-based logistic regression for diabetes risk prediction under severe class imbalance using Wave 5 of the Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS5). The analysis included 115 respondents, comprising 8 diabetes cases (6.96%), with all predictors represented as categorical variables. Model performance was evaluated using 50 repeated stratified 75/25 train-test splits, with SMOTEN applied only to training data to prevent leakage. Standard logistic regression failed to converge across all partitions. Firth's Penalized Logistic Regression identified waist circumference as significantly associated with diabetes status (odds ratio = 10.69, 95% CI: 1.5673.14) and achieved mean accuracy of 89.17%, sensitivity of 8.00%, specificity of 95.19%, and AUC of 0.692. SMOTEN-based logistic regression achieved accuracy of 86.90%, sensitivity of 12.00%, specificity of 92.44%, and AUC of 0.632. Brier scores were 0.089 and 0.098, respectively, compared with 0.064 for the prevalence benchmark, indicating poorer overall probabilistic prediction performance. These findings illustrate the challenges of rare-event prediction under severe class imbalance and highlight the need for larger samples and further validation before clinical application.

title: Sobol and GJR-GARCH for Dominant Factors of European Option Prices in Blue-Chip Index Constituent Stocks
abstractText: Conditional volatility-based option pricing research generally emphasizes improving volatility inputs, but has not yet fully explained the relative contribution of each parameter to variation in simulated option-pricing responses for Indonesian index stocks. This study integrates BlackScholes, GJR-GARCH asymmetric volatility, and Sobol global sensitivity analysis to identify dominant factors in a model-generated European call-option response for verified constituents of an Indonesian blue-chip index, denoted Index X. The sample consists of 19 constituents that remained consistent from February 2022 to December 2025. Logarithmic returns are tested for stationarity and ARCH effects, conditional volatility is estimated using GJR-GARCH(1,1), and the BlackScholes response is evaluated with five independently and uniformly distributed inputs: moneyness, maturity, risk-free rate, volatility multiplier, and proportional transaction cost. The results show that all returns are stationary and most stocks exhibit significant ARCH effects. Under the baseline domain, maturity and moneyness are the leading factors, while the volatility multiplier is secondary and the risk-free rate and transaction cost have smaller contributions. The ranking remains contract-dominated under a wider scenario domain and under a Student-t innovation check, although the magnitudes and ordering of maturity and moneyness can change. The contribution of this research is sensitivity decomposition of a specified BlackScholes response with a GJR-GARCH-based volatility input, not evidence of improved pricing accuracy against observed option prices. Issuer and index identities are masked in the manuscript to prevent issuer-specific model outputs from being misconstrued as investment recommendations or comparative assessments; a confidential identity crosswalk is retained for editorial verification.

title: Secure Runtime Reconfiguration Framework for FPGA-Based Embedded Systems in Mission-Critical Applications
abstractText: Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) have become a popular platform to implement high performance and flexible mission-critical embedded systems with capabilities of configuration at run-time. Nevertheless, although dynamic partial reconfiguration (DPR) is the way to achieve flexibility and resource utilization, this introduces unacceptable security risks, especially in domains where the integrity of system, along with confidentiality and availability are some of the components that cannot be compromised. The theme of the paper is the design of a Secure Runtime Reconfiguration Framework (SRRF) targeted to meet the needs of FPGA-based embedded systems in a mission-critical setting like aerospace, defense, and medical instrumentation. The suggested structure is a combination of a cryptographically safe bitstream management component, a runtime verification and monitoring system, as well as a hardware-assisted tamper risk recognition system that enables secure loading, authentication and legislation of the reconfigurable modules. Confidentiality and integrity Our architecture leverages authenticated encryption (AES-GCM) to provide confidentiality and integrity of bitstreams and an authenticated and cryptographically secured boot chain and reconfiguration controllers (e.g., ICAP/PCAP interfaces). Here, the threat model is carefully examined through the use of the STRIDE and the threat vectors include bitstream spoofing, fault injection, and side-channel exploit. We deploy and test the framework on a Xilinx Zynq-7000 platform in different scenarios of working and attack operation. Cryptographic overhead is minimal (~3.1% latency overhead) and area is spared (< 8 percent LUTs allocated to security interventions) as indicated by experimental results, and it is robust to runtime attacks. The SRRF not only increases the trustworthiness of the system, but also does not come at the expense of performance, therefore, appearing as an attractive solution to high-assurance, reconfigurable embedded implementations. This work contributes towards the state-of-the-art on how to support secure FPGA reconfiguration by presenting a scalable, lightweight and standards-compliant solution in the safety- and security-sensitive fields.

abstractText: In this paper, we introduce an extended two-factor q-differential multiplier operator denoted by ℳq,,n,mf(z). Using this operator, we define the associated subclasses Xq,,n,m() and Yq,,n,m(,) of analytic functions. We obtain upper bounds for the initial coefficients a2, a3 and FeketeSzeg inequalities for the functional |a3 a22| for functions belonging to these subclasses. The bounds are derived by reducing the coefficient problem to standard Carathodory estimates. The estimate for X is sharp, whereas for Y sharpness is established at the Carathodory level and actual extremality is conditional on solvability of the defining differential equation. Additional consequences include third coefficient estimates, a logarithmic coefficient inequality, an upper bound for the second Hankel determinant, and a classical limiting theorem.

Isu Fatherless dalam film “Andai Ibu Tidak Menikah dengan Ayah”. Analisis Framing Robert N Entman
abstractText: The fatherless issue refers to the absence of a father's role in a child's life, both physically and emotionally, which can affect children's psychological, social, and character development. As a mass communication medium, film has the ability to frame various social issues, including the issue of fatherless. This study aims to analyze the framing of the fatherless issue in the film Andai Ibu Tidak Menikah dengan Ayah using Robert N. Entman's framing analysis model, which consists of define problems, diagnose causes, make moral judgement, and treatment recommendation. This research employs a qualitative approach with a constructivist paradigm. The data were collected through observation of scenes, dialogues, characters' expressions, and visual elements in the film, supported by a literature review. The findings indicate that the film frames the fatherless issue as the absence of a father's role in parenting, protection, economic support, and emotional care for children. This condition is influenced by the father's lack of responsibility, online gambling habits, and neglect of the family, leading to conflicts, economic difficulties, and emotional burdens on the children. The film also emphasizes the importance of a father's presence and involvement in family life. Therefore, the film constructs the fatherless issue as a social condition that significantly affects family life and children's development. Future research is expected to explore the topic of fatherlessness using a variety of communication approaches and to raise awareness of the importance of the father’s role in child development

title: Autoconcepto y estrategias de aprendizaje en estudiantes de enfermería
abstractText: Objective: To determine the relationship between self-concept and learning strategies among nursing students. Methods: Quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional correlational study. The population comprised 610 students in the 8th, 9th and 10th academic terms; 236 participants were selected by simple random probabilistic sampling. A version of the AF5 questionnaire assessing academic, emotional and social self-concept and a learning strategies scale covering cognitive and learning-control strategies, learning support, and study habits were administered. Normality was assessed with the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and associations with Spearman's rho. Results: Medium self-concept was observed in 62.3% of participants and medium learning strategies in 68.6%. Overall self-concept was positively and moderately correlated with learning strategies (rho=0.604; p<0.001). Significant correlations were also found for academic self-concept (rho=0.604; p<0.001) and social self-concept (rho=0.418; p<0.001), whereas emotional self-concept was not associated (rho=0.027; p=0.683). Conclusion: Higher self-concept, particularly its academic and social components, was associated with greater use of learning strategies. The cross-sectional design does not allow causal inference. Keywords: self-concept; learning strategies; nursing students; higher education; self-regulated learning.

title: AMP Deaminase-2 Activators and Regulators Underpinning Cellular Function in Human Fructose and Nucleotide Metabolism
abstractText: Abstract AMP deaminase (AMPD) plays an integral role in fructose metabolism via its regulation by ATP, GTP, and phosphate (Pi). The fructose catabolic pathway consumes ATP, producing ADP, which is further metabolized to AMP, triggering a cascade of reactions initiated by AMPD. This degradative pathway results in the final product uric acid, which is associated with metabolic acidosis, mitochondrial dysfunction, and gout. Understanding the regulation of the human liver AMPD isozyme (hAMPD2-2) under physiological conditions and under fructose consumption conditions will enable the design of targeted therapeutics to block the accumulation of uric acid. We report the first successful expression and purification from Escherichia coli of both the full-length and catalytic domains of hAMPD2-2. Steady-state kinetics confirmed allosteric activation by MgATP of both the full-length and catalytic domains of hAMPD2-2 at physiological total ATP concentrations (2–5 mM), suggesting that the allosteric ATP-binding site is located in the catalytic domain. Competitive inhibition by GTP of the ATP-activated enzyme, with Ki values of 74 and 101 μM for the full-length and catalytic domains, respectively, was also consistent with this regulatory model. Pi, previously described in yeast AMPD as a competitive inhibitor, was shown to play a more nuanced role: enhancing inhibition of hAMPD2-2 when the enzyme is complexed to GTP via competition at the ATP allosteric site. Pi binding thus further inhibits the pathway under normal physiological conditions, which suggests that in cells, production of uric acid is limited unless and until Pi and GTP levels are low.

title: A cascaded probabilistic framework for stealth-aware MITRE ATT&CK path prediction in active directory adversary emulation
abstractText: Abstract Proactive adversary emulation requires anticipating multi-step attack trajectories, yet existing approaches rely on static attack graphs or single-signal models that cannot jointly satisfy coherence, tactical realism, and evasiveness. We propose a cascaded probabilistic framework for MITRE ATT&CK technique-path prediction in Active Directory environments, where exhaustive enumeration is intractable. Its contribution is a three-stage architecture that decouples these objectives instead of blending them. Stage 1, a two-layer unidirectional LSTM trained on observed threat-actor chains, emits a five-candidate pool rather than one technique. Stage 2, an empirical Markov tactic-transition gate, admits only attested transitions, including self-loops and backward moves a strict linear kill chain excludes. Stage 3 re-ranks survivors against a detection-rule corpus, favoring evasive over merely probable techniques. Candidates are masked at inference to Windows-applicable techniques, so outputs are technique chains, not instantiated paths. Under a prefix-disjoint protocol in which no evaluation context occurs in training, the true continuation is retained in the five-candidate pool more often than by a first-order predictor or an exact prefix-lookup table on identical pairs. Because Stage 3 both selects on and is scored by detection-rule density, the chains are re-scored against independently maintained corpora the selector never accesses; the exposure reduction persists there, and it is that transferred result that carries the evasiveness claim. Novel here is that structural admissibility is a hard constraint rather than a soft weight, so tactical realism cannot be traded away for likelihood or stealth. A case study initiated from a single initial-access technique further indicates that all tactic transitions within the returned path portfolio have attested support in the corpus transition matrix, and that no predicted step violates the ATT&CK-declared phase set of its technique.

Comparison of the Photodegradation of Pharmaceuticals and Personal Care Products (PPCPs) in Water and Ice
abstractText: Abstract Photochemical reactions are prevalent in natural aquatic environments and play a crucial role in aquatic ecosystems. Sunlight-induced photodegradation is particularly effective in degrading various pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs). However, the photochemical behavior of pollutants within surface ice in cold regions remains unclear. This review synthesizes current research advances regarding the photochemical transformation mechanisms and associated environmental risks of PPCPs in ice, highlighting the significance of these transformations in evaluating the environmental impact of PPCPs in such contexts. In ice or snow, PPCPs may undergo transformation pathways (e.g., photolysis and free radical reactions), which differ from those in aquatic environments. Factors including ice crystal structure, pH, dissolved organic matter, and light conditions can influence their transformation efficiency and the resulting degradation products. This review systematically elucidates the photochemical reaction pathways, key influencing factors, and potential ecotoxicological effects of PPCPs in ice. These transformation processes may generate secondary products that are more persistent or toxic than the parent compounds, posing potential threats to aquatic ecosystems and food chains in cold regions. Therefore, there is an urgent need to thoroughly explore the environmental behavior and ecological risks of PPCPs to provide a scientific basis for pollution control and ecological protection in cold environments.

title: Short-Term Earnings Forecast of CSI 300etf — Based on the Monte Carlo Simulation Method
abstractText: This paper takes Huatai-Pine Bridge Fund Management Co., Ltd's CSI 300ETF(510300) as the research object, selects the real trading data of 300 trading days from June 1, 2025, to March 24, 2026, and uses the Monte Carlo simulation method to research short-term income prediction. Firstly, the core parameters (average daily rate of return -0.007%, standard deviation of daily rate of return 0.662%) are calculated based on historical data, and then 10000 price fluctuation paths are generated through geometric Brownian motion to quantitatively analyze the distribution characteristics of returns in the next 30 days. The empirical results show that the expected total return rate of CSI 300etf in the next 30 days is -0.215%, and the average daily return rate is -0.007%, which is highly consistent with the historical return trend. The 95% confidence interval is [-7.356%, 6.892%], with a rise probability of 47.23% and a fall probability of 52.77%. The gap between the two is small, reflecting that the subject matter has a narrow range of shocks and slight falls in the short term, and the fluctuation risk is controllable. The historical back test verification shows that the prediction error of the model is in a reasonable range, with good adaptability and effectiveness. The research conclusion can provide a quantitative reference for the asset allocation of robust investors, and enrich the empirical research results of broad-based ETF earnings prediction.

title: Taiwanese Bankruptcy Prediction with LASSO and Default-Put-Inspired Random Forests
abstractText: Bankruptcy prediction is a critical but unusually demanding classification problem because failed firms are rare and the cost of a missing is often larger than the cost of a false alarm. This study examines 6,819 Taiwanese firm observations described by 95 financial indicators, of which 220 (3.23%) are labeled bankrupt. Using a stratified 60%/20%/20% split, this study applies LASSO to select 25 accounting variables and compares supervised, ensemble, and anomaly-detection models under a recall-focused measure framework. A repeated LASSO filtering is applied and takes five additional structural-credit features into consideration, including an American default-put value approximated by a neural-network surrogate trained on least-squares Monte Carlo prices and an analytical terminal-shortfall probability; 25 total predictors are again retained. Among baseline models, random forest provides the strongest AUC-precision balance (AUC 0.9548; precision 0.3971; recall 0.6136). The refitted credit proxy-augmented random forest without SMOTE raises average precision from 0.3451 to 0.3790 without changing recall. Its SMOTE variant produces an AUC of 0.9574, average precision of 0.4198, and recall of 0.6364. In conclusion, findings of this paper demonstrate a superior performance for ensemble models (e.g. Random Forest) and an efficient feature engineering framework which can be further extended and integrated under structural credit theory.

In Her Purse: Designing a Benefits Navigation Platform for Incomplete and Sensitive Disclosures
abstractText: Public assistance is organized by program, while people seeking help often describe overlapping needs without knowing which agency or eligibility category applies. In Her Purse is a deployed web platform that accepts a plain-language description and optional profile information to search approximately 4,489 official U.S. assistance listings. This paper examines its Eligibility Matcher as a design for navigation across housing, income, education, employment, and other support domains. The matcher combines semantic retrieval with language-model analysis, presents criteria that appear satisfied separately from those requiring clarification, and requires neither an account nor a complete profile. A descriptive evaluation used thirty written personas situated in economic abuse, including five Spanish- or Chinese-language inputs. The system returned 297 listing instances representing 131 distinct programs, with a reported mean of 3.9 need domains per persona. The evaluation also exposed organizational funding notices among individual-facing results and lower confidence labels for incomplete and non-English inputs. These results establish output coverage in the tested scenarios, not eligibility accuracy, user benefit, or safety. The paper contributes an implemented navigation approach and an account of the design problems that remain when broad program retrieval must support decisions made with limited information.

title: Progress and Challenges in the Application of CAR T-Cell Therapy for Hematologic Malignancies
abstractText: With an aging population and changes in environmental and lifestyle factors, the incidence of hematologic malignancies has been increasing worldwide. Diseases such as leukemia, lymphoma, and multiple myeloma are often characterized by rapid progression and high relapse rates, posing a serious threat to human health. Conventional treatment modalities, including chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and transplantation of hematopoietic stem cells, have demonstrated limited efficacy among individuals with relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies. Drug resistance, low remission rates, and poor prognosis remain major clinical concerns, underscoring the pressing demand for innovative therapeutic approaches capable of addressing the limitations of current treatments. Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR T-cell) therapy is widely regarded as a significant advancement in the field of cancer immunotherapy. Owing to its precise targeting and potent antitumor activity, CAR T-cell therapy has provided a novel treatment option for individuals affected by relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies. Based on relevant literature review and inductive analysis, this review offers a comprehensive overview of recent progress regarding the clinical use of CAR T-cell therapy for a range of hematologic malignancies. It focuses on the major challenges associated with clinical application, particularly cytokine release syndrome, tumor immune evasion, and high treatment costs. In addition, current technological improvements and clinical optimization strategies are discussed, and future development trends are explored. Existing evidence indicates that, compared with conventional treatment modalities, CAR T-cell therapy provides clinically meaningful benefits for individuals with relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies. It can improve remission rates and clinical outcomes and therefore has considerable clinical value. However, several limitations remain, including the risk of serious adverse events, tumor immune evasion, and high costs, all of which substantially hinder its clinical translation and widespread application.

title: School Mediation as an Intervention to Enhance Teachers' Mental Resilience
abstractText: This paper explores the role of school mediation in strengthening the mental resilience of teachers working in high-conflict school environments. While most of the existing literature focuses primarily on students, this study shifts the spotlight to the teachers themselves—those who are often burdened with managing challenging behaviors and resolving school conflicts, a reality that contributes significantly to professional burnout. Through a case study conducted in a secondary school, and based on qualitative data drawn from interviews and observations, the research examines how the implementation of a mediation program affects the participating teachers. The findings suggest that their involvement in the program is linked to reduced emotional exhaustion, increased job satisfaction, and the development of empathy and active listening skills. Mediation emerges not only as a tool for peaceful conflict resolution, but also as a means of personal empowerment for educators. The study concludes by highlighting the need for institutional support and further research across a broader range of school settings.

Topology-optimized dielectric cavities for enhanced excitonic light emission from WSe2
abstractText: Abstract Photonic inverse design and, especially, topology optimization, enable dielectric cavities with deeply sub-diffraction mode volumes and high quality factors, thus offering a powerful platform for enhanced light-matter coupling. Here, we design and fabricate arrays of CMOS-compatible silicon cavities on sapphire with extreme subwavelength transverse mode sizes of only 30–40 nm ( $${{\bf{V}}}{{\boldsymbol{\sim }}}{{{\boldsymbol{\lambda }}}}^{{{\boldsymbol{3}}}}/{{\boldsymbol{2500}}}$$ V ~ λ 3 / 2500 ). These cavities are engineered for deterministic coupling to a monolayer (or few-layer) excitonic material, producing strong near-field localization directly beneath the 2D material. Photoluminescence (PL) measurements show reproducible tenfold raw enhancement relative to bare silicon, which corresponds to a “per-area” normalized enhancement on the order of 10 3 , accounting for the small area of the deeply subwavelength mode volume, consistent with numerical simulations that account for material absorption and fabrication tolerances. Furthermore, time-resolved PL measurements reveal pronounced lifetime shortening and non-exponential dynamics, indicating cavity-mediated exciton-exciton interactions. The optimized cavity geometry enhances the far-field collection efficiency and supports scalable integration with van der Waals semiconductors. Our results show that the arrays of topology-optimized dielectric cavities are a versatile, scalable platform for controlling excitonic emission and interactions, which creates new opportunities in nonlinear optics, optoelectronics, and quantum photonics.

title: Association of Caregiver Mental Health and a Childhood Parenting Intervention in China
abstractText: OBJECTIVES This study examines whether and how caregiver mental health symptoms influence the impacts of a center-based parenting intervention on child development. METHODS We conducted a clustered randomized controlled trial across 100 rural villages in China between 2016 and 2019. Villages were randomly assigned to a treatment group that received weekly 1-on-1 parenting sessions through parenting centers or to a pure comparison group. A total of 2554 caregiver–child dyads with children aged 6 to 24 months were surveyed at baseline, and 2044 completed the endline survey after 1 year (follow-up rate: 80.0%). Child development was assessed using the Bayley Scales of Infant Development, Third Edition. Caregiver mental health was measured using the Depression Anxiety and Stress Scale-21. Ordinary least squares regressions with interaction terms were used for analysis. RESULTS The intervention significantly improved cognitive (β = 0.17 SD; 95% CI 0.045–0.29) and language development (β = 0.10 SD; 95% CI 0.00–0.21) among children whose caregivers did not exhibit depressive symptoms at baseline. Positive cognitive effects were also observed among children of caregivers with low anxiety (β = 0.13 SD; 95% CI 0.00–0.26) or low stress (β = 0.15 SD; 95% CI 0.03–0.27). In contrast, no significant effects were detected across developmental domains among children whose caregivers exhibited mental health symptoms. Heterogeneous impacts were driven by differences in stimulating parenting practices rather than program attendance or parenting beliefs. CONCLUSIONS The intervention primarily benefited children whose caregivers had no baseline mental health symptoms, suggesting caregiver mental health moderates intervention effects.

title: A Deep Nitsche Method for Elliptic Interface Problem with Implicit Jump Condition
abstractText: In this paper, we present a deep Nitsche method for elliptic interface problems involving implicit jump conditions. To approximate the solution with discontinuities across the interface, we employ neural networks augmented with an additional variable to label the subdomains divided by the interface. The neural network solution is obtained by minimizing an energy functional derived from Nitsche’s formula. This approach handles boundary and interface conditions more effectively than typical deep Ritz methods. We establish an optimal error estimate of the proposed method under an inverse inequality assumption on the neural network functions, in the sense that the piecewise $H^1$-error can be bounded above by the best approximation error for the neural networks of the same class. Several numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method.

title: Decoding Philosophers' Misogynistic Remarks on Xiaohongshu: A Discourse Analysis of 1,037 Comments
abstractText: On Xiaohongshu, a Chinese lifestyle platform with a female-majority user base, misogynistic remarks associated with Schopenhauer, Nietzsche, and Rousseau have become recurring objects of public commentary. Drawing on Hall's Encoding/Decoding model and feminist critical discourse analysis, this study uses a qualitative-dominant mixed-methods design to analyze 1,037 individually identifiable comment units from 19 philosopher-centered threads documented between May 2021 and August 2026. After 358 non-attitudinal or unclassifiable units were excluded, 679 comments were coded. Oppositional decoding was largest overall (41.1%), followed by dominant decoding (24.9%), playful de-authoritization (22.2%), and negotiated decoding (11.8%). Opposition predominated in the Nietzsche- and Schopenhauer-centered groups, whereas playful de-authoritization led the Rousseau-centered group (44.0%). Unlike opposition, which challenges propositions or their ideological basis, playful de-authoritization primarily lowers the philosopher's status through memes, slang, bodily or biographical satire, and wordplay. The findings show how platform vernaculars broaden ordinary readers' access to canonical interpretation and reshape epistemic authority.

title: Decoding the Impact of Solvent Hydrogen-Bonding Networks on Nanozyme Activity via Machine Learning Potentials
abstractText: Precise mechanistic insights into the chemical reactions at solid-liquid interfaces are crucial for advancing functional nanomaterials, such as enzyme-mimicking nanocatalysts known as nanozymes. However, conventional periodic density functional theory (DFT) calculations, usually performed under vacuum conditions, can systematically underestimate reaction barriers, leading to discrepancies between computational predictions and the catalytic performance of nanomaterials in aqueous environments. Here, we propose a deep potential (DP)-based strategy that integrates DFT, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and active learning to resolve solvent-mediated reaction kinetics. Using hydrogen peroxide dissociation on Au(111) as a prototypical model reaction for nanozyme activity, we develop a DP model that show comparable accuracy to DFT calculations, enabling efficient identification of transition states in explicit solvents. Calculations using this model have demonstrated that the aqueous hydrogen-bonding network significantly increases the energy barrier for $H_2O_2$ dissociation by 0.58 eV, the experimentally observed low activity of gold nanoparticles in aqueous media. This approach provides a robust framework to decode solvent effects on chemical reactions at solid-liquid interfaces, which is valuable for advancing the rational design of functional nanocatalysts such as nanozymes.

title: Employment, Education, and Psychological Resilience: An Exploration of Role Conflict in Evening School Students
abstractText: This study investigates the relationship between role conflict and psychological resilience among students attending Evening Junior High Schools and High Schools. Its aim is to examine the intensity of role conflict, the level of resilience, and the relationship of demographic and work-related factors with the variables under study. The methodological approach was quantitative, with the use of an open-ended question to provide a complementary account of participants’ observations. Data were collected from 70 individuals (aged 22–56) through a questionnaire combining closed-ended Likert-type items and one open-ended question for comments. The findings indicate high levels of role conflict, with lack of time and physical fatigue emerging as its main dimensions. Psychological resilience was found to range from moderate to high levels, suggesting the presence of strong internal motivation. Statistical analysis revealed a negative correlation between the two variables, indicating that increased role conflict is associated with lower levels of psychological resilience. Finally, factors such as gender, age, and workload appear to differentiate students’ experiences.

title: A Review of Driver Gene Co-mutations in Prognostic Stratification of Targeted Therapy for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
abstractText: EGFR-TKIs have significantly improved the survival outcomes of patients with EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment efficacy exists among individuals, and conventional single-gene testing has limitations in guiding therapeutic decision-making. This systematic review focuses on the effects of driver gene co-mutations on the prognosis of targeted therapy in EGFR-mutant NSCLC and explores their value in clinical translation. Literature published from 2022 to 2026 concerning co-mutations and prognosis of targeted therapy in EGFR-mutant NSCLC was systematically retrieved from the PubMed database for summarization and analysis. This review found that TP53 is the most prevalent co-mutated gene in EGFR-mutant NSCLC and is strongly associated with poor prognosis under TKI monotherapy. Phase III clinical trials have confirmed that TKI combined with chemotherapy significantly prolongs median progression-free survival compared with TKI monotherapy among patients with EGFR mutations accompanied by tumor suppressor gene co-mutations. NGS multi-gene panels serve as the technical foundation for comprehensive co-mutation assessment. In summary, driver gene co-mutations play a critical role in prognostic stratification for EGFR-mutant NSCLC treatment. Taking co-mutation status into account helps identify high-risk patients who may benefit from intensified treatment, supporting more precise and individualized targeted therapy.

title: Cerium Loading Redistributes Tetracycline Removal between Dark Adsorption and the UV Stage on Hydrothermal Niobium Oxide
abstractText: Photocatalysts that also adsorb are usually ranked by how much pollutant disappears at the end of a run, a number that says nothing about which of the two processes did the work. We separate the two on a single material family by running a dark stage and an illuminated stage in sequence and following the solution in-line. Niobium oxide with nominal Ce loadings of 1 %–5 % was prepared in one hydrothermal step from ammonium niobate oxalate and cerium nitrate, and tested against 20 mg L−1 tetracycline under 254 nm irradiation. Total removal after 180 min did not differ significantly across the three compositions, at 53.5 ± 0.7 %, 57.1 ± 1.9 % and 54.2 ± 3.2 % for Ce1%–Nb2O5, Ce3%–Nb2O5 and Ce5%–Nb2O5 respectively (Welch p≥0.19). The dark stage did separate them: uptake before illumination was 24.4 ± 0.7 mg g−1, 36.6 ± 0.8 mg g−1 and 27.5 ± 0.4 mg g−1 (p≤0.047 for every pair, n=2), and the apparent first-order constant of the UV stage fell as dark uptake rose (r=−0.90, p=0.014, n=6). Direct photolysis cannot produce that spread, because it would be fastest where the solution is most dilute, and dark uptake was close to its plateau by lamp-on, so the spread is attributable to the solids. Ce loading therefore redistributes removal between dark uptake and the UV stage rather than changing the total, so a fixed-time removal percentage cannot rank these materials, whereas dark-stage uptake separates them.

title: Understanding Relative Reactivity-Governed Kinetics and Network Formation in Thiol-Yne and Other Competitive Consecutive Polymerizations
abstractText: Abstract Thiol-yne polymerizations couple two sequential additions of thiol: first, to an alkyne and subsequently, to a vinyl sulfide, making the polymerization and the resulting polymer structure dependent on the relative reactivity. Herein, kinetic, analytical, and random-graph frameworks are developed that predict the reaction kinetics and network formation of thiol-yne polymerizations. The kinetic model predicts a chemically driven form of rate acceleration that arises from the interplay between vinyl sulfide generation and consumption and results in the maximum rate being up to 33% faster than the initial rate. Time-independent solutions are found for the conversion trajectories that are then used to derive expressions for gel-point conversion, sol fraction, and elastically active network chain concentrations. The results generalize to other competitive consecutive reactions, such as epoxy-amine reactions. The propagation ratio (γ=kp,enekp,yne) and the stoichiometric ratio of thiol to yne functional groups (χ=[SH0][Y0])are found to govern the relative conversions and network formation, while chain-transfer determines the time scale. In the presence of conversion limitations, the final network develops a kinetic path dependence, transforming the propagation ratio from a transient kinetic property to a governing parameter of the final network structure.

title: Explaining adherence to tuberculosis treatment through the information-motivation-behavioral skills model: a PLS - SEM study in Indonesia
abstractText: Abstract Background Tuberculosis is a serious public health issue because the success of treatment highly depends on adherence. In Serdang Bedagai, 48.87% of patients were reported to take their medication regularly for a period of less than six months. The purpose of this study was to explore the associations between Information, Motivation, and Behavioral Skills within an adapted IMB measurement model among tuberculosis patients in Serdang Bedagai Regency. Method The research uses an explanatory quantitative approach with a cross-sectional survey design. The sample consisted of 230 tuberculosis patients, category 1 as new patients who have never been treated or have taken Anti-Tuberculosis Drugs (OAT) for less than one month, probability sampling with cluster random sampling technique from six community health centers with high, medium, and low case categories. Data were collected using a Likert Scale questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM 3). The measurement model consists of three indicators of Information, three indicators of Motivation, and four indicators of Behavioral Skills. All constructs meet the criteria for reliability and convergent validity, with composite reliability ranging from 0.811 to 0.826 and Average Variance Extracted from 0.523 to 0.614. Results The structural model shows no multicollinearity issues, with a VIF of 1.014. Information and Motivation together explain 8.2% of the variation in Behavioral Skills (R²=0.082), with low but positive predictive relevance (Q²=0.029). Information has a significant negative effect on Behavioral Skills (β=-0.226; t = 3.326; p = 0.001), while Motivation has a significant positive effect (β = 0.151; t = 2.049; p = 0.041). The coefficient of Information is greater than that of Motivation, but the direction of their influence is different, so it cannot be interpreted as a stronger positive influence. Conclusion The adapted IMB measurement model provided exploratory evidence regarding the associations between Information, Motivation, and adherence-related Behavioral Skills among tuberculosis patients. The findings should be interpreted as context-specific structural relationships rather than as evidence that the IMB model fully explains tuberculosis treatment adherence.

title: Differentiated Regulatory Mechanisms of Art Therapy on Brain Health
abstractText: Currently, suboptimal mental health, emotional disorders and traumatic stress disorders are rising year by year, while traditional psychological interventions suffer from homogenization and insufficient targeting. Based on neuroplasticity and the Expressive Therapies Continuum theory, this study systematically analyzes pathological characteristics and repair logic of core brain regions including the prefrontal cortex, amygdala and hippocampus, and compares differentiated neural regulatory effects of four categories of art forms: painting, music, handcraft and passive aesthetic appreciation. The study identifies brain region activation rules and intervention advantages corresponding to each art modality, and distinguishes the varied functions of active creation and passive aesthetic appreciation in emotion regulation, cognitive remodeling and traumatic memory repair. This study makes up for the deficiency that existing research stresses practical effects yet lacks analysis of differentiated action mechanisms. It establishes an intervention framework matching art forms, cerebral regulatory characteristics and crowd demands, and promotes art therapy from experience-based implementation toward more targeted scientific intervention. Future research can adopt multimodal neuroimaging experiments to further quantify intervention thresholds of different art modalities and long-term cerebral functional remodeling rules, so as to improve the precise art therapy system.

title: Mechanisms of Brand Authenticity Erosion in AI-Generated Advertising: A Systematic Review
abstractText: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in advertising since 2022 has transformed content production while raising concerns about the preservation of brand authenticity, a critical foundation of consumer trust and brand relationships. This study examines how AI-generated advertising influences perceived brand authenticity, identifies the mechanisms driving authenticity erosion, and explains the contextual factors that account for inconsistent findings in prior research. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this review synthesizes 13 studies published between 2022 and 2026 retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and EBSCOhost databases. Through thematic synthesis, this study identifies three interrelated mechanisms through which AI-generated advertising may undermine brand authenticity: disclosure effects, failed anthropomorphism, and sincerity erosion. The findings further reveal that the effects of AI-generated advertising on authenticity perceptions are contingent upon individual characteristics, product and brand contexts, and source-related factors, including AI capability beliefs, product type, luxury positioning, and communicator characteristics. This study develops an integrated framework explaining when and why AI-generated advertising enhances or undermines brand authenticity, thus providing theoretical insights for consumer research and practical implications for AI-enabled marketing decision-making.

Trajetória do ensino de enfermagem obstétrica: contribuições de docentes e egressas
abstractText: Objetivo: Historicizar as contribuições de docentes e egressas para a trajetória e consolidação do ensino de Enfermagem Obstétrica na Universidade de Brasília. Métodos: Estudo histórico-social, com utilização da metodologia da história oral, a partir de entrevistas semiestruturadas com duas docentes e três egressas do curso de Enfermagem da Universidade de Brasília. Resultados: As narrativas destacaram a participação das docentes na trajetória do ensino da obstetrícia e na valorização de uma formação humanizada. Nos relatos das três egressas, as experiências acadêmicas e extensionistas foram descritas como elementos relevantes para a escolha da obstetrícia como área profissional. Os depoimentos também permitiram reconstruir marcos institucionais e formativos relacionados ao ensino, à extensão e à continuidade da formação na área. Conclusão: Os relatos analisados indicam que a formação vivenciada na graduação e a atuação docente tiveram papel relevante na trajetória das participantes, contribuindo para a construção de saberes, para a valorização do cuidado humanizado e para a preservação da memória do ensino de Enfermagem Obstétrica na Universidade de Brasília.

title: Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitors: Structural Evolution, Binding Mechanisms, and Theranostic Applications in Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography Imaging
abstractText: α-Fibroblast activation protein (α-FAP) is overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts within the tumor microenvironment of most epithelial cancers, making it an attractive target for cancer-specific imaging and therapy. This article summarizes the structural features, binding mechanisms, radiolabelling strategies, and clinical potential of FAP inhibitors (FAPIs). FAPI molecules generally consist of three functional modules: a quinoline-based core for target recognition, a linker, and a DOTA/NOTA chelator for radionuclide labelling. The interaction between FAPIs and α-FAP is primarily mediated by several amino acid residues, each engaging a specific structural module of the inhibitor, but residues involved are not fixed and may shift with structural variation among FAPI derivatives. The evolution from early boronic acid compounds to UAMC-1110 marks a transition from non-selective dipeptidyl peptidase inhibitors toward FAP-selective warheads, while later modifications (e.g., cyano to α-ketoamide) addressed the need for prolonged target residence. PET/CT is the combination of functional and structural scanning, increasing diagnostic accuracy. The same targeting principle also enables therapeutic applications when labelled with β-emitting radionuclides. The clear specificity of FAPI also helps overcome many limitations of 18 F-FDG.

A Review of Social Media Use, Depressive Symptoms, and Underlying Psychological Mechanisms in University Students
abstractText: As social media has become an integral part of university students' daily lives, its impact on mental health has attracted increasing attention. Against this background, this paper reviews existing research on social media use and depressive symptoms, focusing on overall associations, variations across types of use, and the psychological mechanisms involved. Previous studies have generally indicated that the relationship between social media use and depression is complex rather than simply causal. More specifically, problematic, passive, and addictive forms of use are more strongly associated with psychological risks than general or functional use. At the mechanism level, FoMO and upward social comparison may serve as initial triggers by fostering feelings of inadequacy and negative self-perceptions, which may then be reinforced by envy and rumination, further prolonging negative emotions. Meanwhile, loneliness and limited social support may exacerbate depressive symptoms. Consequently, the impact of social media on university students' mental health is shaped by usage duration, usage patterns, and the psychological processes involved.

abstractText: The continuous professional development of teachers constitutes a critical factor in improving the quality of educational work and responding to the demands of contemporary vocational education. The purpose of this study is to investigate the training needs of teachers of technical and vocational specialties who served at the 1st Laboratory Center of Piraeus, using a quantitative methodological approach through a questionnaire. The findings indicate that teachers primarily seek training in their subject matter and in issues of a psycho-pedagogical nature, while showing a preference for flexible forms of distance learning. The content of the training programs and the scientific competence of the trainers emerge as the most desirable characteristics of in-service training. The main motivation for participation is the acquisition of new knowledge and skills, whereas the lack of free time is identified as the most significant inhibiting factor. Differences related to age and teaching experience are observed mainly among younger and less experienced teachers. The findings of this study can be utilized in the design of targeted training actions in the field of vocational education.

The Role of Technology in Differentiated and Collaborative Learning: Adapting to Learning Styles and Digital Personalization Tools in Primary Education
abstractText: The integration of technology in education has become a decisive factor in shaping contemporary teaching and learning practices. Differentiated instruction and collaborative learning represent two pivotal pedagogical approaches that seek to address classroom diversity and foster active student engagement. The present study aims to examine the role of technology in supporting these approaches within primary education, with particular emphasis on adapting to diverse learning styles and individual learner needs. The research involved 110 fifth- and sixth-grade students from three primary schools and employed a mixed-methods design comprising questionnaires, interviews, and classroom observations. The findings highlight that digital platforms such as Google Classroom, Padlet, and Kahoot enhance participation, facilitate differentiation, and promote interaction. Nevertheless, challenges persist, including unequal access to digital resources and the need for continuous teacher professional development. The study concludes that technology can serve as a catalyst for strengthening differentiated and collaborative learning, provided it is embedded within coherent and pedagogically sound frameworks.

title: Somatic Gene‑Editing Potential and Engineering Barriers for Chronic Cardiovascular Disease Management
abstractText: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are major chronic health conditions, and some patients require long-term medication to control disease progression and associated risks. The need for more durable treatment has therefore significantly increased, leading to importance to find a more long-lasting treatment strategy. This paper examines the potential of somatic gene editing in the foreseeable future, while evaluating the engineering challenges and ethical limitations. Current research demonstrates the potential of somatic gene editing in vivo to modify disease-associated genetic alterations, providing evidence that gene editing could contribute to more durable CVD treatment. However, off-target effects remain the main safety issue, as an accidental change to unintended DNA regions may lead to lethal biological consequences. In addition, safely and efficiently delivering editing agents is an engineering challenge, as precision and capacity have to be both guaranteed. Furthermore, there are ethical issues regarding genetic diversity and social inequalities due to a feasibility of low accessibility to gene editing therapy. Overall, somatic gene editing shows considerable potential to shift the management of selected chronic CVDs towards more durable, mechanism-based treatment, but significant engineering, safety and ethical barriers must be addressed before it can become a reliable alternative to long-term medication.

title: Competing Spin and Charge Symmetry Breaking in the Nematic State of EuFe 2 As 2 Revealed by 57 Fe Nuclear Forward Scattering
abstractText: The electronic and magnetic symmetries of EuFe 2 As 2 at ambient pressure were investigated by combining 57 Fe nuclear forward scattering (NFS) with magnetic-field-induced detwinning. While the magnetic hyperfine field ([Formula: see text]) is consistent with the conventional stripe-type antiferromagnetic (sAFM) configuration, the electric field gradient (EFG) tensor reveals a spontaneous symmetry lowering to monoclinic. Furthermore, this monoclinic distortion persists even in the pressure-induced paramagnetic phase at low temperatures, which is consistent with the asymmetry of the X-ray diffraction peaks. Our findings characterize a unique state arising from an intense competition between the spin-density ([Formula: see text]) and charge-density (EFG) channels. This monoclinic charge-density modulation, coexisting with collinear sAFM order, challenges the conventional orthorhombic picture of iron-based superconductors and provides a new perspective on multi-channel nematic instability.

Research on the Relationship Between Environmental Perception and Personal Moral Judgment: The Moderating Role of Conscientiousness
abstractText: The relationship between environmental orderliness and individual moral judgment has attracted increasing scholarly attention; however, existing studies primarily focus on main effects, with insufficient examination of personality traits as boundary conditions. This study employed a single-factor between-subjects experimental design, using static images of orderly and disorderly classrooms to manipulate the classroom environment variable, and explored the effect of the classroom environment's orderliness on the moral judgment of secondary school students, as well as the moderating role of conscientiousness. A total of 217 valid .responses were collected. Moral judgment was measured using six campus-life scenarios on a 7-point scale, and conscientiousness was assessed with the two-item Conscientiousness dimension of the Ten-Item Personality Inventory (TIPI). An independent-samples t-test and a two-way ANOVA were conducted for data analysis. Results showed that the main effect of environmental orderliness on moral judgment was not significant, t(215) = 0.71, p = 0.4785; the interaction effect between environmental orderliness and conscientiousness also failed to reach statistical significance, F(1, 213) = 1.108, p = 0.2938. Neither Hypothesis H1 nor H2 was supported. The results indicate that the static picture-priming paradigm may not be ecologically valid for adolescent samples and that the mechanism involved in the processing of moral judgment is quite different from that involved in overt deviant behavior. This study offers an empirical basis for selecting paradigms in future studies and provides descriptive findings on the potential threshold effect in conscientiousness moderation.

Intelligent Technologies for Urban Rail Transit Emergency Management
abstractText: With the increasing urban rail transit network and the closer connection among operational subsystems, the potential influence range and management difficulty of emergencies have greatly increased. The current emergency management based on traditional methods has some shortcomings in real-time risk recognition, integration of multi-source information and cross-departmental collaborative decision-making. By integrating a comprehensive literature survey with typical case analyses, this paper investigates the use of Internet of Things (IoT), big data, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twins (DTs) in urban rail transit emergency management. The research is carried out from three main aspects: risk monitoring and early warning, emergency decision-making and collaborative response, and passenger evacuation and operation recovery. The results show that intelligent techniques offer assistance in the monitoring of operational status, anomaly detection, emergency information exchange and evaluation of evacuation plans, which can effectively improve the processing efficiency of information and the supportive ability in decision-making. However, at present, the actual implementations are limited by insufficient data sharing between different systems, restricted model generalization, lack of validation in practical operational situations, and network and data security risks. In the future, more efforts should be made to standardize multi-source data and sharing mechanisms, strengthen the validation of intelligent models and DT systems under real operational conditions, and optimize human-in-the-loop collaborative decision-making to improve the reliability and practicability of intelligent technologies in urban rail transit emergency management.

title: Family accommodation is associated with childhood social anxiety disorder and anxiety symptom severity
abstractText: Abstract Parenting processes are thought to shape children’s emotional development and may be particularly relevant once childhood social anxiety disorder (SAD) is clinically established. This study examined two distinct parenting processes—family accommodation (FA), a symptom-linked response to child anxiety, and challenging parenting behavior (CPB), a broader autonomy-promoting parenting dimension. Cross-sectional questionnaire and diagnostic interview data were drawn from three clinically characterized samples comprising youth with SAD ( n = 121), specific phobia ( n = 65), and healthy controls ( n = 147; total N = 333). Parents reported on FA and CPB using validated measures. Parents of youth with SAD reported greater FA than parents of healthy children, whereas CPB did not differ between groups. Higher FA was consistently associated with greater child SAD/anxiety severity, whereas CPB was unrelated to symptom severity. In two-parent families, FA and CPB showed little evidence of cross-parent coupling. Exploratory comparisons did not indicate that either parenting process differentiated SAD from other anxiety disorders. Overall, among the two parenting processes examined, symptom-linked accommodation showed the more consistent pattern of association with clinically established childhood SAD and anxiety severity, supporting its relevance for parent-focused assessment while leaving causal direction and broader diagnostic specificity beyond anxiety disorders unresolved.

title: Selective preoperative lower extremity computed tomography angiography before mandibular reconstruction: Identifying patients unlikely to require fibula free flap reconstruction
abstractText: Abstract Purpose Not every patient undergoing mandibular continuity resection requires free fibula flap (FFF) reconstruction. Whether clinical judgment reliably identifies patients unlikely to benefit from preoperative lower-extremity computed tomography angiography (CTA) remains unknown, despite the relevance of this question for cost-conscious and resource-efficient imaging strategies. Methods A retrospective outcome-based validation was conducted in patients undergoing mandibular continuity resection between July 2012 and June 2023. The primary outcome was secondary FFF reconstruction among patients not initially selected for CTA. Factors associated with CTA utilization were assessed by multivariable logistic regression. Results 316 consecutively operated patients were included. Prior radiotherapy (OR 2.67, p = 0.005) and smoking history (OR 1.98, p = 0.032) were independently associated with CTA utilization. Among 111 patients without primary FFF reconstruction, four (3.6%) required secondary FFF reconstruction, all of whom had undergone CTA. No patient managed without CTA subsequently required FFF reconstruction. Conclusions In this cohort, clinical judgment was associated with successful identification of patients who did not subsequently require fibular reconstruction. Omission of CTA in carefully selected patients was not associated with subsequent reconstructive deficiency, though larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: IMPLEMENTASI PEMBELAJARAN MENDALAM MELALUI PROJECT-BASED LEARNING YANG DIDUKUNG AI-BASED MICROLEARNING TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR TEKNIK KOMPUTER DAN JARINGAN PADA MATERI SERANGAN SIBER KELAS XI SMK MUHAMMADIYAH 1 PEKANBARU
abstractText: This study was motivated by the low learning outcomes of students in the cyberattack topic in the 11th-grade Computer and Network Engineering (TKJ) class at SMK Muhammadiyah 1 Pekanbaru. This study aimed to describe the implementation of Deep Learning through the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model supported by AI-Based Microlearning and to analyze changes in students’ learning outcomes after the implementation of the learning approach. The study employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental method with a One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. The participants consisted of 25 students from the 11th-grade TKJ class. Data were collected through learning outcome tests, product assessments, presentation assessments, and documentation. The data were analyzed using normality tests, the Paired Sample t-Test, N-Gain, and effect size analysis using Cohen’s d. AI-Based Microlearning was used as conceptual reinforcement by presenting concise learning materials on the types, characteristics, impacts, and prevention of cyberattacks before students conducted case analyses, participated in group discussions, and completed projects in the form of educational posters and presentations. The product assessment score for the posters was 88.3%, while the presentation assessment score was 90.3%, both categorized as very good. These scores reflected students’ achievement in project activities and were not used as the sole indicators of the overall implementation of the learning process. The mean learning outcome score increased from 61.46 in the pretest to 83.39 in the posttest. The Paired Sample t-Test showed a significant difference between the pretest and posttest scores (p < 0.001). The mean N-Gain score was 0.569, categorized as moderate, while Cohen’s d of 1.43 indicated a large effect size. These findings indicate that the implementation of Deep Learning through PjBL supported by AI-Based Microlearning was associated with improved student learning outcomes; however, the improvement cannot be fully attributed to the intervention because the study did not employ a control group. The integration of these three approaches may serve as an alternative strategy for contextual and problem-solving-oriented learning in Computer and Network Engineering. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya hasil belajar peserta didik pada materi serangan siber di kelas XI Teknik Komputer dan Jaringan (TKJ) SMK Muhammadiyah 1 Pekanbaru. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan implementasi Pembelajaran Mendalam melalui model Project-Based Learning (PjBL) berbantuan AI-Based Microlearning serta menganalisis perubahan hasil belajar peserta didik setelah penerapan pembelajaran tersebut. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode pra-eksperimen dan desain One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 25 peserta didik kelas XI TKJ. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes hasil belajar, penilaian produk, penilaian presentasi, dan dokumentasi. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas, Paired Sample t-Test, N-Gain, dan ukuran efek menggunakan Cohen’s d. AI-Based Microlearning digunakan sebagai penguatan konsep dengan menyajikan materi singkat mengenai jenis, karakteristik, dampak, dan pencegahan serangan siber sebelum peserta didik melakukan analisis kasus, diskusi kelompok, serta menyelesaikan proyek berupa poster edukasi dan presentasi. Hasil penilaian produk poster sebesar 88,3% dan presentasi sebesar 90,3%, keduanya berkategori sangat baik. Kedua hasil tersebut menggambarkan capaian peserta didik dalam aktivitas proyek dan tidak digunakan sebagai satu-satunya indikator keterlaksanaan keseluruhan pembelajaran. Rata-rata hasil belajar meningkat dari 61,46 pada pretest menjadi 83,39 pada posttest. Hasil Paired Sample t-Test menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan antara skor pretest dan posttest (p < 0,001).
