Integrasi ketiga pendekatan tersebut dapat menjadi alternatif strategi pembelajaran TKJ yang kontekstual dan berorientasi pada pemecahan masalah.

title: RISK OF PANCREATITIS FOLLOWING ENDOSCOPIC ULTRASONOGRAPHY: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
abstractText: Endoscopic ultrasonography-guided tissue sampling is widely used to diagnose pancreatic lesions, but pancreatitis remains a clinically relevant adverse event, and evidence on its risk factors is inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to summarize the incidence of pancreatitis after endoscopic ultrasonography and to evaluate patient- and procedure-related risk factors. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies reporting pancreatitis after endoscopic ultrasonography and evaluating risk factors. Risk factors reported in at least two studies with extractable dichotomous data were pooled as risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals using the Mantel–Haenszel fixed-effect model. Five studies were included: two cohort studies, a multicenter pooled analysis, a retrospective case–control study, and a case report. The reported incidence of pancreatitis ranged from 0.29% to 9.2%, reflecting differences in study populations and procedural risk. Only two studies provided data suitable for pooling. Pancreatitis was not significantly associated with sex (risk ratio 1.13; 95% confidence interval 0.48–2.64), history of pancreatitis (1.50; 0.60–3.75), or sampling of the pancreatic head versus other locations (1.21; 0.50–2.94), and no between-study heterogeneity was observed. In individual studies, recent acute pancreatitis and side-branch intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm were associated with a higher risk. Pancreatitis after endoscopic ultrasonography-guided pancreatic sampling is uncommon, and its reported incidence varies with patient selection and procedural characteristics. The pooled findings are limited by the small number of studies and participants. Recent pancreatitis and needle passage through the pancreatic duct or normal parenchyma may identify patients at higher risk and warrant prospective investigation.

title: Peran Disposisi Matematis dalam Meningkatkan Kemampuan Berpikir Kritis dan Komunikasi Matematis
abstractText: Disposisi matematis merupakan salah satu faktor afektif yang berperan penting dalam menentukan kesiapan siswa untuk berpikir kritis dan mengomunikasikan gagasan matematis secara efektif. Tujuan dari penelitian ini adalah untuk mendeskripsikan bagaimana peran disposisi matematis dalam meningkatkan kemampuan berpikir kritis dan komunikasi matematis siswa. Metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan deskriptif interpretatif akan digunakan pada penelitian ini. Adapun subjek penelitiannya adalah siswa kelas XI SMAN 98 Jakarta yang dipilih secara purposif untuk mewakili kategori disposisi matematis tinggi, sedang, dan rendah. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket disposisi matematis, tes tertulis kemampuan berpikir kritis dan komunikasi matematis, serta wawancara semi terstruktur. Selanjutnya data akan dianalisis melalui tahap reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa siswa dengan disposisi matematis tinggi mampu menunjukkan indikator berpikir kritis secara lebih lengkap, meliputi interpretasi, analisis, evaluasi, dan inferensi, serta mampu mengomunikasikan ide matematis secara runtut baik secara tertulis maupun lisan. Siswa dengan disposisi sedang menunjukkan capaian yang belum konsisten, terutama pada aspek pemberian alasan logis, sedangkan siswa dengan disposisi rendah cenderung bergantung pada hafalan prosedural dan mengalami kesulitan mengungkapkan penalaran matematisnya. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa disposisi matematis berperan sebagai fondasi afektif yang mendukung berkembangnya kemampuan berpikir tingkat tinggi dan kompetensi komunikasi dalam pembelajaran matematika. Penelitian ini merekomendasikan agar guru secara sengaja menumbuhkan rasa percaya diri, keingintahuan, dan ketekunan siswa melalui pembelajaran berbasis masalah terbuka dan diskusi untuk memperkuat kemampuan berpikir kritis dan komunikasi matematis secara bersamaan.

Induced abortion and its associated factors among female students in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstractText: Abstract Objective To assess the pooled prevalence of induced abortion and its associated factors among female students in sub-Saharan Africa. Method Comprehensive literature searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, The Health Internetwork Access to Research Initiative (HINARI), African Journals Online, and Google Scholar. Articles published from January 1, 2000, to March 30, 2025, were included. Both peer-reviewed published articles and grey literature were included in this review. Two authors extracted all relevant data using a standardized data extraction format in a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet, which was then exported to Stata 17 for analysis. Meta-analysis was conducted using the Der Simonian and Laird random-effects model. Sensitivity analysis was performed to assess the effect of a single study on the overall prevalence. Subgroup analysis and meta-regression were conducted to explore potential sources of heterogeneity. A funnel plot and Egger’s test were used to assess publication bias, which was addressed using trim-and-fill analysis. Result A total of 41 primary studies involving 18,741 female students were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalence of induced abortion among female students in the sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) region was found to be 13% (95% CI: 9%–18%). In the subgroup analysis, female students from the western sub-region had a higher prevalence compared to other sub-regions. Additionally, tertiary-level students had a higher prevalence of induced abortion compared to secondary-level students. Alcohol consumption was a significant factor associated with induced abortion in this study. Conclusion Female students in sub-Saharan Africa experience a high prevalence of induced abortion, with subgroup analyses indicating higher rates in West Africa and among tertiary students compared with secondary students. Alcohol consumption was associated with induced abortion. These findings should be interpreted with caution due to limitations in study design, small numbers of studies for some factors, and substantial heterogeneity. Nevertheless, the study provides preliminary evidence to inform future research and guide context-specific interventions.

abstractText: This study explores the attitudes, level of familiarity, and use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools among school principals in secondary education in Greece. title: The Influence of Airfoil Geometric Parameters on Lift Generation Mechanisms: An Analysis Based on Aerodynamic Principles
abstractText: Through geometric optimization, airfoil designs directly affect efficiency, stability, and energy performance in aerospace and wind systems. More specifically, airfoil geometry optimization improves aerodynamic efficiency and reduces energy losses in aircraft and wind turbines, thus supporting technological innovation and cleaner energy utilization. This paper examines the physical mechanisms of lift generation and evaluates the influences of key airfoil geometric parameters, including maximum thickness, maximum camber, their chordwise locations, and trailing-edge configurations, on lift performance. To explain these effects, the analysis examines lift mechanisms from classical inviscid circulation models, including the Kutta-Joukowski theorem and thin-airfoil theory, to viscous-flow frameworks describing boundary-layer transition, shear stress distribution, and vorticity dynamics. At low Reynolds number conditions (0.3×10⁵ to 0.8×10⁵), viscous effects become significant and produce laminar separation bubbles that reduce aerodynamic efficiency. The results show that airfoil geometric parameters regulate lift generation mainly by reshaping surface pressure distributions and modifying boundary-layer stability, providing a physics-based foundation for optimized lifting surface design.

title: Analysis of Success Factors in the Use of Audit Application in the Implementation of Audit Tasks at PT XYZ Using the DeLone & McLean
abstractText: Background: The successful implementation of the Audit Management System (TeamMate and IDEA) in the Internal Audit Division of PT XYZ, an Indonesian financing company, depends on several factors. This study applies the DeLone & McLean (2003) Information Systems Success Model to assess System Quality, Information Quality, Service Quality, User Satisfaction, and Net Benefits. Objective: This study aims to assess the factors associated with the successful implementation of the Audit Management System in PT XYZ’s Internal Audit Division. Methods: The study used a quantitative design based on questionnaires administered to internal auditors. The population consisted of 95 active TeamMate users, including managers, supervisors, and audit staff. Using stratified random sampling, 85 respondents were determined through statistical power analysis for Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), assuming a medium effect size (0.15), 90% statistical power, a 5% significance level, and a maximum of four structural paths. Measurement items were adapted from validated information-systems research. A pilot test involving 15 TeamMate users was conducted to assess item clarity and response consistency. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 3. Results: System Quality and Service Quality significantly increase User Satisfaction. User Satisfaction also significantly contributes to Net Benefits, particularly through increased audit efficiency and improved reporting accuracy. Conclusion: Continuous improvements in technical infrastructure, system quality, and support services are essential for strengthening user satisfaction and maximizing organizational benefits, thereby supporting sustainable digital audit transformation.

title: On Artificial Intelligence as Assistive Technology in Archaeological Scholarship
abstractText: In archaeological scholarship, the challenge of interpreting large amounts of fragmented evidence can be daunting. This paper will examine how artificial intelligence can assist in this process, mainly through examining visual evidence and classifying material evidence. Drawing from Trevor Paglen's argument of machine vision and Matteo Pasquinelli's history of classification in machines, this paper develops an analysis of two archaeological case studies: archaeological site detection based on satellite imagery in Mesopotamia and deep-learning classification of Tusayan White Ware pottery. The findings of the studies demonstrate that artificial intelligence is capable of expanding preliminary surveys as well as applying typologies consistently. At the same time, they also highlight the importance of human input, coming to the conclusion that artificial intelligence's potential and principal contribution lies in simplifying the archaeological process and directing human attention towards evidence requiring further interpretation, establishing a framework for understanding artificial intelligence as an assistive technology.

title: Research on Multi-source Data Fusion Quality Risk Prediction Model for Drug Registration Compliance
abstractText: Drug registration compliance management faces practical challenges such as complex submission documents, dispersed risk sources, and diversified review stages. Traditional manual review methods have difficulty identifying potential quality risks in a timely manner, especially when cumulative risk is formed by cross source, cross stage, and cross type information. Against this background, a multi source data fusion quality risk prediction model was developed for the drug registration scenario. The model integrated submission and review texts, historical deficiency records, inspection results, manufacturing change information, and regulatory provisions. Unified preprocessing, feature extraction, fusion modeling, and stratified training were then applied to achieve risk level identification. The results showed that the multi source fusion model outperformed single source models in Accuracy, Recall, F1, and AUC. Among them, the fusion XGBoost model achieved the best overall performance and significantly reduced the miss rate of high risk cases. The interpretability analysis further indicated that historical deficiency frequency, regulatory terminology deviation rate, abnormal inspection ratio, and manufacturing change density were the key factors affecting risk judgment. This study provides a computable, verifiable, and early warning oriented technical path for drug registration compliance management, and offers more targeted digital support for enterprise pre review and regulatory assisted assessment.

Statistical Measurement of F1 Fan Attention Dynamics: Competitive Performance, Media Exposure, and Social Interaction
abstractText: With the expansion of F1 racing across social media, search platforms, and streaming media, driver attention has gradually become a continuously observable data point. Existing research typically uses Google Trends, fan size, fan growth, and engagement rate to measure changes in attention, but these indicators correspond to search attention, cumulative audience, and immediate engagement, respectively, and their statistical meanings are not interchangeable. Regarding driving factors such as competitive performance, race suspense, media exposure, and social interaction, relevant literature employs methods such as linear regression, count regression, panel models, event studies, and nonparametric tests. Existing evidence shows that F1 fan attention exhibits time dependence, long-tail distribution, cardinality effects, and platform heterogeneity, and there is also endogeneity between media exposure and competitive performance. Statistical analysis requires first distinguishing between Search, Growth, and Engagement, then selecting a model based on the distribution of the dependent variable and the data structure, and controlling for individual differences and time impacts through fixed effects, event windows, and robust standard errors. This establishes an analytical path from indicator measurement and driving factors to dynamic identification, providing a statistical foundation for the quantitative comparison of F1 fan attention and subsequent driver-level panel analysis.

Building Sandstones in Germany – Shaping Landscapes and Cultural Heritage
abstractText: Abstract Sandstones are found close to the surface in large parts of central Germany and have been quarried and used there for many centuries. From a stratigraphic point of view, clastic sediments occur from the Cambrian to the Quaternary periods; the building sandstones mainly belong to the Upper Paleozoic and the Mesozoic. The use of sandstone has been documented since the Stone Age, with systematic quarrying beginning in south-western Germany with the Romans and in other regions at the end of the Middle Ages in the 11th /twelfth century. Current studies on building sandstone in Germany suggest that over the centuries there have been tens of thousands of quarries and extraction sites for building sandstone. In all these regions, the cultural landscapes are characterised by sandstone—the landscape and buildings merge to create a harmonious view. Sandstones can be found in secular buildings, in many walls, along paths and, of course, in representative buildings such as churches, monasteries, castles, town halls and later buildings from the industrial age such as railway stations, factory headquarters, etc. Some of these cultural landscapes extend along the rivers on which the sandstone was transported, especially to the northern parts of Germany. 15 of the 55 UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Germany consist mainly of sandstone and owe their special character to it. Sandstone also occurs to a lesser extent at 16 other UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The cultural heritage not only represent material, cultural, architectural and historical value, but are also part of what makes our ‘old’ continent of Europe – the ‘Museum of Europe’. Monument preservation in Germany takes these aspects into account and sets high standards for the material and professional preservation and restoration of these stone cultural assets. This is based on knowledge of the petrographic and petrophysical properties of sandstones as well as the history of their extraction and use. In a long-term project, the Federal Institute for Geosciences and Natural Resources (BGR) is systematically investigating building sandstones in Germany in collaboration with the geological surveys of the federal states as well as universities and institutions. The results are published for each federal state and are available to users in the field of monument preservation. A brief summary of the results of this comprehensive project to date is presented here. The results include a series of publications presenting all building sandstone deposits in Germany by federal state in a geological-stratigraphic context with their petrographic and petrophysical properties, as well as the results of research into historical quarrying and use, building sandstone and thin section collections in various institutions, data collections on historical quarries, analyses and other information, the development of a non-destructive method for analysing the provenance of building sandstones and, last but not least, the impetus for non-geologists to pay more attention to building sandstones and their provenance and features in buildings.

title: Research on Enterprise Financial Risk Intelligent Early-Warning Model Based on XGBoost
abstractText: Against the background that the demand for risk prevention and control in the capital market is increasingly prominent, financial crises of listed companies occur frequently. Traditional linear early warning models find it difficult to depict the nonlinear associations of financial indicators, and also face practical problems such as sample imbalance and model black box. This paper selects A-share non-financial listed companies, constructs a multi-dimensional financial early warning indicator system, uses period t indicators to predict period t+1 financial risk, constructs a financial risk early warning model based on XGBoost, introduces SHAP to realize the interpretable analysis of the model, and conducts comparative empirical research with logistic regression and random forest. The results show that the XGBoost model has better overall accuracy and early warning precision, and profitability, cash flow, and solvency indicators are the core factors for identifying financial risk; SHAP can effectively solve the model black box problem, and realize global risk factor identification and single-enterprise risk tracing. The research can provide technical support and decision-making reference for enterprise management, investors, creditors, and regulatory agencies to carry out financial risk identification and risk control.

title: TOGAF-Guided Microservice Architecture for Scalable and Interoperable Madrasah Learning Portals
abstractText: Purpose – This study aims to design and evaluate an integrated madrasah learning portal by combining The Open Group Architecture Framework (TOGAF) with microservice architecture to improve the scalability, modularity, and interoperability of academic information services. Methods – The study employed selected TOGAF Architecture Development Method phases to align business, data, application, and technology requirements. The proposed architecture decomposed academic functions into User, Learning, and Assessment Services connected through REST APIs. Academic datasets representing students, teachers, subjects, classes, attendance, assignments, and assessments were used for proof-of-concept implementation. The architecture was evaluated through workload-based backend processing, cross-service identifier consistency, simulated workload iterations, and exploratory comparisons with monolithic architectural scenarios. Findings – The proposed architecture successfully integrated core academic services through modular service decomposition and standardized communication mechanisms. The workload evaluation demonstrated stable processing behavior under lower workloads, while larger workloads required increased execution time. Cross-service data relationships maintained consistent identifier references across the evaluated academic datasets. The exploratory architectural comparison also indicated that the Microservice + TOGAF configuration provided more efficient backend processing behavior than the evaluated monolithic configurations within the controlled environment. Research Implications – The proposed model provides a reference architecture for educational institutions seeking structured, modular, and interoperable academic information systems. Originality – This study integrates TOGAF-guided enterprise architecture with microservice-based academic service decomposition and evaluates the resulting architecture through scalability and interoperability analyses in a madrasah learning context.

Hasil Belajar Materi Perubahan Iklim dengan Media Pembelajaran Berbasis Android pada Siswa Kelas X
abstractText: Penelitian ini menelaah hasil belajar kognitif siswa kelas X pada materi perubahan iklim setelah pembelajaran menggunakan media berbasis Android. Kajian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh keterbatasan variasi media pembelajaran di kelas dan oleh bukti terdahulu yang menunjukkan bahwa manfaat mobile learning dipengaruhi oleh desain pedagogis, konteks materi, dan cara implementasinya. Penelitian menggunakan kuasi eksperimen dengan desain nonequivalent pretest-posttest control group pada 70 siswa SMA Negeri 3 Mataram, masing-masing 35 siswa pada kelas eksperimen dan kontrol. Kelas eksperimen menggunakan media Android yang dikembangkan dengan Construct 2 selama empat pertemuan, sedangkan kelas kontrol mengikuti pembelajaran tanpa media tersebut. Hasil belajar diukur menggunakan 25 soal pilihan ganda. Secara deskriptif, rata-rata pretest kelas eksperimen dan kontrol masing-masing 54,85 dan 45,37, sedangkan rata-rata posttest masing-masing 91,78 dan 84,68. Namun, gain mentah kelas eksperimen (36,93) lebih kecil daripada kelas kontrol (39,31), sehingga perbedaan posttest tidak dapat langsung ditafsirkan sebagai efek perlakuan tanpa mengendalikan perbedaan awal. Oleh karena itu, analisis antar-kelompok perlu menggunakan ANCOVA dengan posttest sebagai luaran dan pretest sebagai kovariat serta melaporkan interval kepercayaan dan ukuran efek. Temuan deskriptif menunjukkan peningkatan pada kedua kelas, tetapi klaim kausal dibatasi sampai analisis yang disesuaikan terhadap baseline tersedia. This study examines Grade X students’ cognitive learning outcomes on climate change after instruction supported by Android-based learning media. The study was motivated by limited variation in classroom learning media and by prior evidence showing that the benefits of mobile learning depend on pedagogical design, subject context, and implementation. A quasi-experimental nonequivalent pretest-posttest control-group design involved 70 students at SMA Negeri 3 Mataram, with 35 students in each group. The experimental class used Android-based media developed with Construct 2 across four meetings, whereas the control class learned without the Android media. Learning outcomes were assessed using 25 multiple-choice items. Descriptively, the experimental and control groups had mean pretest scores of 54.85 and 45.37 and mean posttest scores of 91.78 and 84.68, respectively. However, the experimental group’s raw gain (36.93) was lower than the control group’s raw gain (39.31). Therefore, the higher experimental posttest mean cannot be interpreted directly as a treatment effect without accounting for baseline differences. Between-group inference should use ANCOVA with posttest as the outcome and pretest as the covariate, accompanied by confidence intervals and an effect-size estimate. The descriptive evidence indicates improvement in both groups, while causal claims should remain limited until baseline-adjusted analysis is available.

The Influence of Career Development and Performance Allowances on the Performance of Civil Servants via Work Motivation and Job Satisfaction
abstractText: Civil servant performance is a key determinant of public service effectiveness. However, improving performance cannot rely solely on administrative policies; it also requires organizational support and the strengthening of employees’ psychological conditions. This study aims to examine the effects of career development and performance allowances on employee performance, with work motivation and job satisfaction positioned as mediating variables among civil servants in the Regional Government of North Sumatra Province. The study employed a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design. Data were collected from 414 respondents selected through purposive sampling using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and were analyzed using SPSS 26 and AMOS through Covariance-Based Structural Equation Modeling (CB-SEM). The findings indicate that career development and performance allowances have positive and significant effects on work motivation and job satisfaction. Furthermore, both psychological variables were found to have positive and significant effects on employee performance. These findings suggest that career development and performance allowances enhance employee performance by strengthening work motivation and job satisfaction. Therefore, improving civil servant performance requires the integration of an objective and structured career development system with a fair, transparent, timely, and performance-based allowance policy.

Marine Insurance: Frequency–Severity Claim Modeling and the Effect of Delay on Ruin Probability
abstractText: Reporting dates do not identify claim payment times. We quantify a reporting-based payment-time assumption's effect on finite-horizon cash ruin in an idealized marine portfolio. The freMarine calibration comprises 1,109 positive-payment snapshot claims over 41 occurrence months, with negative-binomial monthly counts, finite-mixture severity, and empirical zero-inflated reporting lags. Refitted-bootstrap diagnostics assess distributional adequacy; conflicting severity diagnostics and rejected parametric lag fits remain explicit. Event-driven simulation couples immediate and proxy payments on the same occurrences and severities, with constant aggregate premiums and an empty initial system. For 250,000 paired paths over 60 months at initial surplus 2,000 EUR thousands, cash-ruin estimates are 0.2951/0.2363 for immediate/proxy payment. The paired difference is -0.0588 (95% conditional Monte Carlo interval [-0.0597,-0.0579]); mean outstanding payments are 718.79 EUR thousands. Nonnegative delay mechanically favors coupled cash surplus without discharging liabilities. Unobserved payment histories, opening claims, and policyholder behavior preclude claims of predictive superiority, a preferred handling policy, or regulatory capital needs.

title: Network-on-Chip Technology for Chiplet Integration Architecture
abstractText: In today's era, the marginal benefits of transistor scaling are continuously decreasing, and Chiplet heterogeneous integration has become the mainstream path for scaling AI chip computing power. Meanwhile, on-chip interconnect performance is increasingly becoming the key factor limiting system computing power and energy efficiency. This paper focuses on on-chip network technology for Chiplet-integrated AI chip architectures, providing a systematic review and analysis of its technical principles, research status, existing limitations, and development directions. The study first breaks down the on-chip network's dual-layer architecture of 'physical architecture layer - protocol mechanism layer,' clarifying the functional roles of each core hardware unit and protocol mechanism and the complete data transmission logic. Next, from the perspectives of topology, routing algorithms, switching mechanisms, and flow control mechanisms, it summarizes the evolution of on-chip network technology and the customized research results for AI computing features and Chiplet heterogeneous scenarios. It then identifies two core current issues—inter-chiplet interconnect performance bottlenecks and lack of cross-layer collaborative design, as well as insufficient dynamic load adaptation and lagging industry standards — and outlines the key paths for future technology optimization. This research can provide clear insights into the technological development path for researchers in the field and offer theoretical support and direction for the interconnect architecture design and industrial implementation of the next-generation highly integrated AI chips.

title: Investigating emotional intelligence and its relationship with academic performance of graduate students
abstractText: The primary objective of this study is to investigate Emotional Intelligence (EI) in the academic context and its contribution to academic performance. EI was analyzed according to the four dimensions of the corresponding model, as well as their effects on students’ performance. The research highlighted the importance of EI for academic and professional success, emphasizing that it constitutes a critical differentiating factor between high-performing professionals and ordinary employees. The study was based on a psychometric questionnaire administered to postgraduate students, with data analyzed using IBM SPSS. The results indicated a positive orientation toward well-being, but weaknesses in self-regulation, emotionality, and sociability. The COVID-19 pandemic may have influenced participants’ optimism; however, the literature suggests that developing EI can enhance performance and support the Greek educational system.

title: A Comparative Study of Deep Time-Series Models for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Health Prediction
abstractText: Model rankings in battery SOH prediction can change with the input representation and battery split. This study therefore evaluated five deep time-series models—Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), PatchTST, TimesNet, and ModernTCN—on the NASA battery aging dataset under chronological and cross-battery protocols using the same input pipeline. The chronological protocol predicts later cycles of B0005, B0006, and B0007, whereas the cross-battery protocol trains on these three batteries and evaluates on the unseen B0018 battery. All models use the same 20-cycle input window and 14 cycle-level features derived from voltage, current, temperature, discharge duration, and historical capacity. The prediction target is the one-step-ahead SOH, defined as \(C_t/C_0\). Each configuration was trained with five random seeds (42–46), and the results are reported as the mean ± sample standard deviation. Under chronological evaluation, GRU achieved the lowest mean MAE, \(0.02513 \pm 0.00708\), while PatchTST obtained the lowest mean RMSE, \(0.03429 \pm 0.00851\), and the highest mean \(R^2\), \(0.73132 \pm 0.13911\). On the unseen B0018 battery, TimesNet performed best, achieving an MAE of \(0.01726 \pm 0.00394\), an RMSE of \(0.02213 \pm 0.00438\), and an \(R^2\) of \(0.88631 \pm 0.04139\); ModernTCN produced closely comparable results. The best model depended on the split: GRU achieved the lowest chronological MAE, whereas TimesNet achieved the best mean performance on the unseen B0018 battery. Removing historical capacity improved some architectures but degraded others, and the direction of the change also depended on the evaluation protocol. Because the cross-battery evaluation uses one held-out battery, these findings should be interpreted as evidence of protocol sensitivity rather than as a universal ranking of the models.

Pengembangan Media Digital Articulate Storyline pada Materi SPLDV
abstractText: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya hasil belajar siswa pada materi SPLDV. Hal ini diketahui dari hasil tes siswa kelas VIII yang menunjukkan bahwa sebanyak 90,91% siswa memperoleh hasil belajar yang rendah. Oleh karena itu, media pembelajaran digital digunakan sebagai solusi untuk mengatasi rendahnya hasil belajar siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui karakteristik media digital articulate storyline yang valid dan praktis, serta mengetahui efektivitas penggunaannya pada materi SPLDV di kelas VIII SMP Negeri 4 Simpangkatis ditinjau dari hasil belajar siswa. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Research and Development (R&D) dengan pengembangan model ADDIE (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, dan Evaluation). Subjek penelitian terdiri atas 66 siswa kelas VIII yang terlibat pada tahap pengembangan dan implementasi. Teknik pengumpulan data meliputi wawancara, angket respon, dan tes. Teknik analisis data menggunakan kriteria pensekoran untuk menilai kevalidan dan kepraktisan media, sedangkan efektivitas media dijelaskan melalui uji ShapiroWilk untuk normalitas data dan uji Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test untuk membandingkan hasil belajar siswa. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa media yang dikembangkan memenuhi kriteria sangat valid dengan persentase sebesar 90,31% dan kepraktisan media tergolong cukup praktis dengan persentase 79,69%. Karakteristik media alur cerita artikulasi digital meliputi soal berdasarkan konteks kehidupan sehari-hari, umpan balik otomatis, dan interaktivitas menyeluruh. Hasil uji Wilcoxon menunjukkan adanya perbedaan yang signifikan antara nilai pretest dan posttest dengan effect size sebesar -1,00 yang termasuk dalam kategori sangat besar. title: Feature-Enhanced Fusion and Adversarial Domain Adaptation for Cross-Condition Few-Shot Fault Diagnosis of Bearings
abstractText: Rolling bearings are core components of rotating machinery, and their operational status is critical to the safe and reliable service of major equipment. However, the variable rotational speeds and loads in industrial environments cause significant data distribution drift; coupled with an extreme scarcity of labelled fault data under new operating conditions, this leads to a severe decline in the generalization performance of traditional deep learning models based on the assumption of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data. To address the dual challenges, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on Feature Enhancement Fusion and Adversarial Domain Adaptation (FEF-ADA). Firstly, a time-frequency spectrum is generated via the Continuous Wavelet Transform, and high-dimensional, discriminative fault features are deeply extracted whilst suppressing industrial background noise through a combination of hollow convolution, spectral convolution and a channel-spatial dual attention mechanism; secondly, a domain adversarial network with a gradient reversal layer is introduced to align the feature manifolds of the source and target domains via a maximum-minimum game mechanism, thereby extracting operating-condition-invariant representations; finally, prototype learning is introduced in the metric space to establish accurate classification decisions relying solely on a very small number of target-domain support samples. Experiments demonstrate that, under conditions of only 15 samples per class (15-shot), FEF-ADA achieved an average recognition rate of 89.70%, with a standard deviation of just 0.70% across five independent experiments. Its performance significantly outperforms traditional CNNs (73.41%), ProtoNet (78.66%) and DANN (82.47%), demonstrating excellent resistance to operating condition drift and significant engineering practical value.

Mechanisms and Biomedical Applications of Sustained- and Controlled-Release Drug Delivery Systems
abstractText: Sustained‑release and controlled‑release drug carriers represent valuable pharmaceutical tools that help boost treatment outcomes while simplifying clinical medication schemes. Unlike conventional immediate‑release tablets and capsules, these systems can moderate or adjust how active pharmaceutical ingredients get released inside organisms. Such features extend therapeutic action durations and lower daily dosing frequencies. This review sorts out core definitions and distinguishing traits of sustained‑release and controlled‑release dosage forms, alongside common product categories and their underlying release mechanisms. Three widely adopted technical solutions are discussed: matrix‑type, membrane‑coated and osmotic‑pump tablet systems. The text addresses their clinical strengths including stable in‑vivo drug levels, reduced dosing frequency and enhanced patient adherence. Real‑world clinical applications covering cardiovascular illnesses, metabolic syndromes and pain management are also summarized. Collectively, sustained‑release and controlled‑release technologies offer feasible pathways to optimize drug delivery and therapeutic performance. Further research into novel excipient materials and delivery techniques is likely to achieve more accurate drug release behaviours and expand the scope of clinical use for such formulations.

Psychosocial implications of online violence in adolescence and clinical intervention strategies in school.
abstractText: Cyber violence is a modern phenomenon of social pathogenesis, which has been of concern to educators and social scientists in recent years, as it can significantly affect sensitive developmental phases of humans, such as adolescence. However, this social phenomenon, although now occurring quite frequently, has not yet been adequately studied, creating a gap in the existing bibliography. The purpose of this article is to study the phenomenon of cyber violence in adolescence, through the investigation of the opinions of Secondary Education teachers, studying, mainly, its psychosocial impact on the victims, but also to propose ways of preventing and dealing with the phenomenon, mainly by social workers working in education. To implement the purpose of this article, a quantitative survey was conducted with a sample of 159 teachers of the S.E. in Kavala, the results of which are presented and followed by a discussion and commentary on the interesting findings, compared to the few pre-existing studies on this phenomenon.

title: Analysis of the Relationship Between the Proportion of Surface Atoms and Light Emission Competition in Semiconductor Nanomaterials
abstractText: Because of their quantum size effects and surface effects, semiconductor nanomaterials show a wide range of optical properties, making them a core part of strategic industries like high-definition displays, solid-state lighting, and biomedical detection. Its light-emitting mechanism mainly includes exciton emission and defect emission. The coexistence and competition between the two is one of the key factors affecting performance. But traditional studies mostly attribute it separately to quantum size effects and surface effects, lacking a unified structural parameter. This article introduces 'surface atom ratio' as a parameter to uniformly describe this competitive relationship, and also analyzes its role as a bridge connecting quantum size effects and surface effects. Using a theoretical analysis approach, starting from the three major effects of nanomaterials, the aim is to derive the relationship between the proportion of surface atoms and size, and explain their connection to enhanced quantum confinement and defect state density; through systematically analyzing the effects of size and surface passivation on competition, the rules of luminescence competition centered on the proportion of surface atoms are summarized. This article found that this parameter can indeed effectively regulate the coexistence and competition between the two, and provides a reference for designing nanomaterials with high luminescence efficiency in a measurable way.

title: Perbandingan kinerja teknik sampling ATR-FTIR dan DRS-FTIR untuk identifikasi mikroplastik PE, PP, PS, dan PET
abstractText: Mikroplastik merupakan polutan persisten yang banyak ditemukan di lingkungan dan memerlukan metode identifikasi yang akurat untuk menentukan jenis polimernya. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan karakteristik spektral yang diperoleh dari dua konfigurasi sampling FTIR, yaitu Attenuated Total Reflection (ATR) dan Diffuse Reflectance Spectroscopy (DRS), pada polimer mikroplastik polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), dan polyethylene terephthalate (PET) dalam bentuk pejal dan serbuk, serta mengevaluasi pengaruh bentuk sampel terhadap baseline dan fitur puncak pada kondisi pengukuran yang digunakan. Sampel mikroplastik diperoleh dari limbah plastik pascakonsumsi yang disintesis menggunakan metode solvent dissolution-precipitation. Karakterisasi dilakukan menggunakan ATR-FTIR dan DRS-FTIR pada rentang bilangan gelombang 4000–400 cm⁻¹ dengan resolusi 4 cm⁻¹ dan 40 kali pemindaian. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh sampel menampilkan puncak serapan karakteristik yang sesuai dengan literatur, meliputi gugus CH₂ pada PE, gugus CH₃ pada PP, cincin aromatik pada PS, serta gugus karbonil ester dan C–O–C pada PET. ATR-FTIR menghasilkan spektrum dengan baseline yang lebih baik pada rentang 95–100 %T dan intensitas serapan puncak yang jelas (transmitansi mencapai 20 %T pada 1715 cm⁻¹ untuk PET dan 756 cm⁻¹ untuk PS). Sementara itu, DRS-FTIR menunjukkan performa yang baik pada sampel PP serbuk dengan puncak karakteristik yang lebih jelas. Pada DRS-FTIR terjadi distorsi optik pada sampel pejal dengan lonjakan baseline mencapai 130–250 %T, serta penurunan baseline pada sampel serbuk hingga 20 %T. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ATR-FTIR merupakan metode sampling yang menghasilkan kualitas spektrum paling optimal, ditandai dengan garis dasar (baseline) yang stabil (95–100 %T) dan puncak serapan karakteristik yang jelas untuk sampel PE, PS, dan PET, baik dalam wujud pejal maupun serbuk. Sebaliknya, DRS-FTIR menunjukkan puncak karakteristik yang lebih baik khusus pada sampel PP berwujud serbuk, tetapi mengalami distorsi optik (baseline 130–250 %T) pada sampel pejal akibat pantulan spekular.

title: Optimizing Antibiotic Duration for Pneumonia and Sinusitis in the Pediatric Emergency Department
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Updates to national and international guidelines now recommend shortening antibiotic durations to 3 to 5 days for uncomplicated community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and 5 to 7 days for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis (ABRS). We aimed to increase the percentage of children discharged home from the emergency department with CAP or ABRS who were treated with an optimal antibiotic duration from 13% to 70% by July 2025. METHODS We assembled a multidisciplinary team and used quality improvement tools, including cause-and-effect analysis, driver diagram, and prioritization matrix, to identify impactful interventions. We also surveyed prescriber comfort with shorter antibiotic durations. Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles included implementing new clinical pathways (CP), electronic health record (EHR) updates, and educating prescribers. Our outcome metric was the percentage of patients receiving recommended antibiotic duration for CAP and ABRS. Process metrics included use of CP Quick Response codes and CAP “Quick-Discharge” order sets. Balancing metric was the number of return visits with the same diagnosis within 14 days. RESULTS We saw shifts in the outcome metric center line in August 2023, February 2024, and November 2024 from 13.1% to 64.8%. These changes primarily reflected CAP duration because it was the more common diagnosis, although ABRS short antibiotic durations showed similar improvement during this time frame. Process metrics showed an increase over time. There was no change in balancing metric. CONCLUSION We significantly improved antibiotic prescription durations for CAP and ABRS through CP changes, EHR updates, prescriber education and feedback, and resource distribution.

title: Deep Learning-Based Calligraphic Aesthetic Assessment Guided by Gestalt Psychological Features
abstractText: Calligraphic aesthetic assessment requires the information about local stroke appearance and the spatial organization of the complete character. This paper develops a supervised regression method that combines twelve Gestalt-inspired geometric descriptors with a ResNet50 image encoder. The descriptors quantify the visual balance, ink distribution, reflected structure, projection rhythm, and distance-transform smoothness. Two feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) modules convert these measurements into channel-wise scales and shifts for intermediate convolutional features. A direct-concatenation control supplies the same descriptors to the regression head. This design allows explicit geometric information to interact with the learned visual representations during score prediction. In the ResNet50 experiment, intermediate FiLM achieves PCC 0.7067 and MAE 1.3554, compared with 0.6958 and 1.3793 for image-only regression. In whole-work assessment, combining local window-score statistics with global layout descriptors achieves PCC 0.6323. These results support descriptor-guided regression at the character level and the combination of local appearance with global composition for whole-work assessment.

title: Implementing A Constructivism-Situated Learning Model of Chinese Pre-service Kindergarten Teachers: Observed Outcomes in Problem-solving and Collaboration Skills
abstractText: Problem-solving and collaboration skills are widely recognized as essential competencies for pre-service kindergarten teachers, yet Chinese teacher preparation programs have struggled to bridge the gap between theoretical instruction and practical application. This study reports the implementation outcomes of an eight-component instructional model grounded in constructivism and situated learning theory. The intervention was delivered over one academic semester to 36 second-year preschool education students in China. Using a one-group pre-test-post-test design, problem-solving skills were measured before and after the intervention, while collaboration skills were assessed at five time points during instruction. Because no control or comparison group was included, the findings are interpreted as observed changes associated with the instructional model rather than as causal effects. Results showed that the total problem-solving score changed from 71.69 to 79.11 (t = 13.28, p < .001, Cohen’s d = 2.21). Collaboration skills exhibited a stepwise pattern across five dimensions, with score rates rising from 66.60% to 96.60%. Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of dimension (F = 432.62, p < .001, partial η² = 0.925). A consistent pattern emerged across both skill areas: behavioral-level competencies showed larger observed gains than deeper-level qualities, suggesting that these deeper capacities may require longer cultivation periods. These implementation findings offer preliminary evidence for integrating constructivist and situated learning principles in pre-service teacher education. They should be interpreted with caution given the single-group design, single intact class, and reliance on observer/self ratings. Future controlled and multi-source studies are needed.

abstractText: Based on experimental materials for a simple pendulum that provide only chart images and include no raw numerical data files, this paper distinguishes theoretical derivations from qualitative image-based observations and explores how time series can be used to represent calculus relationships in periodic motion. The experimental setup described in the materials uses the Arduino Nano 33 IoT development board, the LSM6DS3 inertial measurement unit, and Bluetooth transmission, covering five pendulum lengths from 0.34 m to 1.45 m, with an approximate sampling frequency of 100 Hz. Based on the small-angle simple pendulum model, the analysis establishes the relationship among angular displacement, angular velocity, angular acceleration, period and frequency, and examines the oscillation interval, release shock, decay behavior and multi-axis response in the records. The results show that the images qualitatively support the theoretical trend of "longer pendulum length, slower oscillation", but they are not enough to verify the measured frequency, damping constant or three-dimensional displacement. The study also illustrates how differentiation amplifies noise and why double integration depends on calibration, initial conditions, and drift control. This case provides an intuitive example for establishing links between functions, derivatives, integrals, differential equations, and observable motion characteristics in physics teaching.

title: Recent Advances in the Application of Small-Molecule Fluorescent Probes for Bisulfite ( H S O 3 - )
abstractText: Bisulfite ( H S O 3 - ) serves as an effective preservative in food industry and plays an important role in endogenous cellular redox balance. However, excessive intake of bisulfite into humans may induce a series of complications such as allergic asthma, cardiovascular diseases and neurological disorders. Consequently, it is essential to develop a method to monitor the bisulfite levels in foods and cells. In recent years, small-molecule fluorescent probes for bisulfite detection have emerged as an advanced technology due to their high selectivity, sensitivity and reliability, moreover, they have been utilized in fluorescence imaging for real-time visualization of bisulfite in living tissues and organisms. This review provides a general introduction into the practical applications of these fluorescent probes from 2022 to 2026, exhibiting several advanced detection methods for bisulfite in various samples and the improvements in probe performance. Furthermore, we discuss about certain aspects in probe applications that requires optimization, which can serve as a direction for in-depth researches in the future.

title: Empowering students in the digital age: A gamified approach to GDPR education through Erasmus+
abstractText: This article describes the design, implementation, and evaluation of an educational intervention within the framework of the Erasmus+ program, focusing on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Despite the critical importance of the regulation in the digital age, young people’s understanding of its basic principles remains limited, highlighting the so-called “privacy paradox.” The intervention adopted an experiential pedagogical approach, combining the co-creation of digital materials (infographics, interactive videos) with the development of a decision-making game (gamification) to simulate digital dilemmas. The central objective was to transform complex legal provisions into applied knowledge, while simultaneously strengthening students’ critical stance toward digital privacy. The effectiveness of the method was evaluated through pre-test and post-test questionnaires. The findings demonstrated a statistically significant increase in understanding of the principles of the GDPR (from 15% to 85%), while a substantial enhancement of participants’ self-efficacy and professional readiness was also recorded. The study highlights the superiority of game-based learning in bridging the gap between legal theory and everyday digital practice.

Fairness perceptions and union intentions among U.S. workers: Evidence of a cognition action gap
abstractText: Public approval of unions in the United States has risen to levels not seen in decades, yet union membership remains near historic lows. This study examines whether workers' perceptions of organizational justice explain this representation gap. Drawing on organizational justice theory and the concept of union instrumentality, we surveyed 600 U.S. wage and salary workers, evenly divided between union members and nonmembers, and retained 593 usable responses. Analysis proceeded in three stages: descriptive and Mann Whitney Wilcoxon comparisons, stability selected LASSO network analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis followed by multigroup structural equation modeling with invariance testing. Distributive justice and union instrumentality were empirically indistinguishable and were combined into a single Justice Instrumentality construct. Procedural justice strongly predicted Justice Instrumentality (standardized β = .76 to .80), but neither procedural justice nor Justice Instrumentality significantly predicted union orientation, and explained variance in union orientation was minimal (R² ≈ .01). Structural paths were equivalent across union and nonunion groups. These results suggest that fair procedures shape beliefs about what unions can deliver without translating into pro union intentions, a pattern we term the cognition action gap. Because the design is cross sectional and measures intentions rather than behavior, the gap should be treated as a proposition for longitudinal testing. We discuss implications for employers and for union organizing strategy.

Deciphering Cellular and Spatial Regulatory Identities from Sparse Chromatin Accessibility Landscapes
abstractText: Abstract Chromatin accessibility profiling provides a powerful view of regulatory landscapes across heterogeneous biological systems, enabling the investigation of cell-state diversity and spatially organized regulatory programs. However, deciphering meaningful regulatory identities from sparse and noisy accessibility landscapes remains challenging, particularly for closely related cellular states and neighboring regulatory domains. Unlike transcriptomic measurements, chromatin accessibility does not directly capture canonical marker expression, and regulatory identities must therefore be inferred from indirect evidence, including gene activity scores, transcription factor motif activity, and reference-based annotation. These signals often become ambiguous, limiting the reliability of unsupervised clustering followed by post-hoc interpretation. Here, we present CASSIA (Chromatin Accessibility Semi-Supervised Identity-Aware representation learning), a unified label-guided framework for decoding cellular and spatial regulatory identities from chromatin accessibility landscapes. CASSIA leverages limited high-confidence anchors to learn informative accessibility representations while preserving intrinsic regulatory structures. The framework integrates a binary accessibility denoising autoencoder, a Jensen–Shannon divergence-based clustering constraint, and a similarity difference-aware triplet objective; spatial neighborhood consistency is further incorporated to preserve regulatory organization when spatial information is available. Across diverse chromatin accessibility datasets, CASSIA reconstructs cellular and spatial regulatory identities with improved agreement to biological annotations and tissue organization compared with representative baselines. Identity-associated accessible regions and transcription factor activity profiles reveal distinct regulatory programs underlying inferred identities, demonstrating that CASSIA transforms sparse accessibility landscapes into interpretable cellular and tissue-level regulatory maps.

title: Community Connectedness and Its Association with Stigma and Viral Suppression Among MSM with HIV: Findings from HPTN 078
abstractText: Abstract Gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (MSM) continue to be disproportionately affected by HIV in the United States, with viral suppression rates among MSM across varied racial and ethnic groups remaining below national targets. Stigma is a major barrier to viral suppression, while community connectedness may serve as a protective factor. However, few studies have examined whether different forms of community connectedness are associated with viral suppression or moderate the negative effects of stigma. Data were drawn from 490 MSM with HIV enrolled in the HIV Prevention Trials Network (HPTN) 078 study (2016–2017). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Exploratory moderation analyses tested interactions between stigma and community connectedness, and significant interactions were further examined using stratified models. Viral suppression was documented in 78% ( n = 383) of participants. Having a medium-sized MSM network (6–25 vs. low [0–5 MSM known personally]) was associated with lower odds of viral suppression, whereas medium (2–5) and high (> 5) levels of recent peer interactions (vs. low [0–1]) were associated with higher odds of viral suppression. Perceived connectedness to the broader lesbian, gay, among MSM across varied racial and ethnic groups bisexual(LGB) community was not significantly associated with viral suppression. Exploratory analyses suggested that the association between provider-related MSM stigma and viral suppression may vary by levels of network size and peer interactions, with associations observed only at medium levels of connectedness. These findings suggest that fostering active peer interactions may improve viral suppression among MSM.
